Уха по-фински 🐟 вкусный супчик 🍲 
• голова и хвост для яркого рыбного вкуса.
(рыба может быть любая красная и даже белая)
•морковь- 1 шт +1 шт для бульона
•лук белый -1 шт +1 шт для бульона
•картофель- 2 шт средних
•специи по вкусу -соль /перец
•сливки 20% -300 мл

Готовим 🌿: 
🐟 Отварить голову и хвост 30 минут с луком и морковью , снимая пенку. Посолить. Не давать кипеть , чтоб бульон не получился темным.

🐟В это время обжариваем лук , морковь и картофель до полуготовности. Солим , перчим.

🐟По готовности бульона вынимаем части рыбы. Разделываем. Мясо нарезаем и отправляем обратно в бульон. Туда же следом идут обжаренные овощи. 

🐟Варим ~10 минут. Далее добавляем теплые сливки и доводим до кипения. Выключаем сразу. Добавляем укроп. 

Дайте супу настояться ~15 минут и подаём , изумительно вкусно , обязательно готовьте 🫶

Frying raw pasta—it sounds strange… until you try it🍝 In a dry pan, the pasta takes on an amber hue and a nutty flavor, and once you add mushroom broth, it cooks to perfection. All the ingredients are right in your pantry.

Fun fact: drying mushrooms concentrates their umami — the soaking water ends up stronger than any stock cube.

INGREDIENTS (serves 2–3)
- 9 oz spaghetti, broken up
- 1.5 oz dried mushrooms
- 3 cups hot water (~175°F)
- ½ onion + 3 garlic cloves
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tbsp cold butter
- ½ cup grated parmesan
- Salt to taste

METHOD
1. Soak mushrooms 20 min, squeeze, chop. Strain the liquid — sand sits at the bottom. Keep it hot.
2. Toast the dry pasta in a dry pan till amber and nutty. Set aside.
3. Oil, mushrooms, onion till golden, garlic.
4. Pasta back in, stock to just cover, low heat till it reduces to a sauce.
5. Heat off: cold butter + parmesan, stir to glossy 🧈

🍜 Caramelized Onion Coconut Ramen

Creamy, spicy, nutty ramen with jammy caramelized onions, coconut milk and crispy tofu.

Ingredients

For the caramelized onion coconut broth

* 2 medium onions, thinly sliced
* 1 tbsp butter
* 1–2 tsp chili oil, or to taste
* 1 tbsp soy sauce
* ½–¾ cup coconut milk
* ½–1 cup water or ramen cooking water

For the creamy ramen base

* 1 medium–large egg yolk
  I used 2 because my eggs were small
* 1–1½ tbsp Kewpie mayo or any good-quality egg mayo
* 1–2 tsp chili oil
* 1 tbsp good-quality peanut butter
* 1–2 tsp soy sauce
* Seasoning, to taste
* 1 tsp Buldak cheese seasoning, 
* rice vinegar

For the tofu & toppings

* Crumbled tofu
* Oil
* Salt
* Fresh chilies
* Ramen noodles
* Jammy eggs
* Spring onions
* White and black sesame seeds

Method

1. Caramelize the onions:
 Heat butter in a pan and add the sliced onions. Cook over medium-low heat until they soften, release their moisture and begin to shrink and turn golden brown.
2. Add chili oil and continue cooking until the onions are deeply golden and caramelized.
3. Add soy sauce, then pour in the coconut milk and water/ramen cooking water. Mix well and keep the broth hot.
4. Make the creamy base:
 (You don’t have to cook this base) In a large bowl, add the egg yolk, Kewpie mayo, chili oil, peanut butter, soy sauce and your seasoning. Add the Buldak cheese seasoning . Mix everything until smooth.
5. Add the hot broth:
 Pour the warm caramelized onion coconut broth into the egg-yolk mixture while continuously whisking. Do not put the bowl back on the heat or simmer it. The heat from the broth gently cooks and emulsifies the yolk, creating a silky, creamy broth.
6. Add your cooked ramen noodles and mix everything together until the noodles are beautifully coated in the creamy broth.
7. For the crispy tofu:
 Sauté crumbled tofu in a little oil with salt and fresh chilies until slightly crispy and crumbly.
8. Top the ramen with crispy tofu, jammy eggs, spring onions, and white and black sesame seeds.

And you’re done. 🤌🏼🍜

Most mushroom pastas rely on cream to create richness. This one builds deep flavour with roasted garlic, miso, and butter. 

Ingredients (serves 2–3)

• 250 g pasta
• 2 cups mushrooms (cremini, shiitake, or mixed)
• 1 shallot, finely sliced
• 5–6 cloves garlic
• 1–2 tbsp white miso
• 500 ml chicken or vegetable broth
• 2 tbsp butter
• Olive oil
• 1 cup Parmigiano Reggiano
• Salt & black pepper

Method

1. Roast garlic with olive oil and salt until soft, sweet, and easy to squeeze.
2. Add olive oil and butter to a pan over low heat. Cook shallots until fragrant.
3. Add mushrooms and cook down until they release their moisture and become deeply caramelized.
4. Squeeze in the roasted garlic and mix into the mushrooms.
5. Add miso and stir until it melts into the base, building that deep umami flavour.
6. Add broth and bring everything together.
7. Add pasta directly into the pot and cook until al dente, adding more broth if needed.
8. Turn off heat and finish with Parmigiano Reggiano and butter.
9. Toss until glossy and creamy.

A Japanese ingredient completely changed the way I make mushroom pasta.

This is aglio e olio with roasted red pepper. It’s slowly becoming one of my favourites. 

Ingredients (serves 2–3)

• 250 g spaghetti
• 2 large red bell peppers
• 10-14 cloves garlic
• ½ cup olive oil
• ½–1 cup reserved pasta water
• 1 small handful fresh parsley
• Salt & black pepper
• Parmigiano Reggiano, optional

Method

1. Add the red pepper and olive oil to an oven-safe pan and roast at 425°F (220°C) for 25–30 minutes, turning halfway through, until softened and lightly charred.
2. Gently confit the garlic on low heat in olive oil over for 30 minutes or until soft and golden.
3. Transfer the confited garlic and roasted red pepper to a blender with a spoon of the infused olive oil and blend until completely smooth.
4. Cook the spaghetti in well-salted water until al dente, reserving some pasta water.
5. Add the remaining garlic-infused oil to a pan and toss in the cooked pasta.
6. Add a splash of reserved pasta water and toss vigorously until the oil and pasta water emulsify into a glossy sauce.
7. On low heat add the roasted red pepper sauce.
8. Toss everything together until the sauce coats every strand of pasta.
9. Off the heat finish with freshly chopped parsley and adjust.

Cauliflower Falafel with Herby Yoghurt & Quick Pickled Cabbage

Served with a tangy herb yoghurt, quick pickled cabbage, a handful of fresh herbs and a splash of hot sauce.
Note: Soak 200g dried chickpeas overnight which will double to 400g.  If you forget to soak. Boil chickpeas for 5mins. Pop on a lid, turn off the heat, and leave to sit for one hour. 

Serves 4–6

Falafel
400g soaked chickpeas 
200g cauliflower, roughly chopped
1 tsp ground cumin
1 tsp ground coriander
½ tsp smoked paprika
4 garlic cloves
Pinch of salt
½ bunch flat parsley
½ bunch coriander
Finely grated zest of 1 lemon
1 small onion, finely diced
Olive oil, for shallow frying

Herby Yoghurt
250g natural yoghurt
2 tbsp  chopped mint
2 tbsp chopped coriander
grated zest of 1 lime
1 tbsp lime juice
1 small garlic clove, finely grated
Salt and pepper

Quick Pickled Cabbage
¼ red cabbage, finely sliced
Juice of 1 lime
Pinch of salt

Method
For the herby yoghurt, combine the yoghurt, herbs, lime zest, lime juice and garlic in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper and refrigerate until needed.
For the pickled cabbage, pop the cabbage, lime juice and salt in a bowl. Mix and set aside.
Place the chickpeas, cauliflower, cumin, coriander, paprika, garlic, salt, parsley, coriander and lemon zest into a food processor. Pulse to a coarse paste. 
Transfer to a bowl and fold through the diced onion. Taste a small amount of the mixture and adjust the seasoning if needed.
Shape into small patties.
Heat a generous amount of olive oil in a frying man on med- high heat.
Cook the falafel in batches for 4–5 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden brown and crisp on all sides.
Serve with the herby yoghurt, quick pickled cabbage, warm pita, fresh herbs and hot sauce.

🛒 INGREDIENTS:
Servings: 1
- Soba noodle: 1 bundle 
- Aubergine: 100g
- Leek: 100g
- Radish: 100g
[Sauce]
- Water: 100 ml
- Soy sauce: 1 1/2 tbsp
- White wine: 3 tbsp
- Sugar: 2 tsp
[Topping]
- Chives

🧑‍🍳 METHOD:
1. Simmer sauce ingredients in a pan to burn off alcohol.
2. Grate radish.
3. Cut aubergine into bite-sized pieces and leek into 5cm pieces.
4. Heat oil in a pan and shallow-fry aubergine and leek over medium heat until browned.
5. Toss hot aubergine and leek in sauce to coat.
6. Boil soba noodles, rinse under cold running water, and place on a plate.
7. Top soba with aubergine, leek, grated radish, and chives; pour sauce over and serve cold with ice.

💡 KEY POINTS:
- In this recipe, we’re swapping traditional Sake and Mirin for white wine and sugar in a certain conversion formula. As a Japanese home cook, I assure you it works perfectly to replicate the authentic taste. Only one simple rule you need to follow: 👉 Make sure to use a DRY and LOW-ACIDITY WINE (e.g. Pinot Gris). A cheap one is fine, but avoid using fruity wine.

⛩️ TRADITIONAL OPTION:
- Swap 3 tbsp white wine for 1 1/2 tbsp sake and 1 1/2 tbsp mirin, and reduce sugar from 2 tsp to 1/2 tsp.
- Swap Radish for Daikon radish.

This is my fav one pot recipe when you need some thing fast, creamy coconut dal x john

Serves 4

2 tbsp olive oil
3 tsp cumin seeds
2 onions, finely sliced
4 cloves garlic, finely sliced
1 inch ginger, finely sliced
1 tsp turmeric
1 tsp chilli powder
200g red lentils
1 x400g tin chopped tomatoes
1 x 400g tin coconut milk
The juice of a lime
A small handful of finely chopped coriander leaves
Salt

1. Heat the oil in a saucepan over a medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and crackle for a few seconds before adding the onion. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until golden.
2. Chuck the garlic and ginger into the pan and mix well. Cook, stirring continuously, for 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Put the turmeric, chilli powder, lentils, tomatoes, coconut milk and a good pinch of salt into the pan. Pour in 150ml of just boiled water and mix well. Bring to the boil, cover, reduce the heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, for 25-30 minutes or until the lentils are tender. If it looks a little dry, add another 50-100ml of water and mix well.
4. To finish, add the lime juice and coriander to the daal. Mix well. Check the seasoning, adding more salt to taste and serve immediately with rice.

Full Recipe↓ Day 61/100 | SALMON CHAZUKE

🛒 INGREDIENTS:
Servings: 1
- Rice: 150g
- Salmon: 1 fillet (80g)
[Seasoning for salmon]
- Salt: pinch
- Soy sauce: 1/2 tbsp
- Sesame oil: 1 tsp
[Broth]
- Water: 400ml
- Ginger: 1 knob
- Scallion (Green part): 1
- Salt: 1/4 tsp
- Green tea: 1 tea bag
[Topping]
- Nori seaweed
- Toasted sesame seeds
- Chopped scallions

🧑‍🍳 METHOD:
1. Slice the unpeeled ginger.
2. Separate the scallion greens from the whites, then finely chop the white parts.
3. Season the salmon fillet with salt.
4. Pan-sear the salmon until golden brown on both sides and cooked through.
5. Peel off the crispy skin, leaving it in the pan, and transfer the cooked salmon to a tray or a plate.
6. Flake the salmon meat and toss with soy sauce and sesame oil.
7. Reheat the pan with the salmon skin over medium heat until crisp. Add water, the sliced ginger, scallion greens, and salt.
8. Cover with a lid and simmer on low heat for 10 minutes to extract the flavours.
9. Strain the broth into a jug or teapot and steep a green tea bag for 2-3 minutes.
10. Place warm rice in a bowl, arrange the flaked salmon, chopped scallion whites, toasted sesame seeds and nori over the top, then pour the hot tea broth around it to serve.

💡 KEY POINTS:
- Chazuke (Ochazuke) is traditionally made with dashi broth (like kombu or katsuobushi). Since authentic Japanese dashi isn't always available in everyday European supermarkets, we're building our own umami base using what we have: crispy salmon skin, ginger, and scallion tops

⛩️ TRADITIONAL OPTION:
- Instead of making broth from salmon skin, ginger, and scallion greens, use kombu dashi.

PRAWN FRIED RICE 🦐🍚 Getting very excited to be back in Taiwan next month hosting my own food tour… so I thought it was only right to bring back one of my favourites 🇹🇼

Prawns
- 10 large fresh prawns
- 1 tsp veg oil
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/2 tsp white pepper
- 1/4 tsp baking soda

Fried Rice
- Veg oil, to cook
- 2 cups white rice, day old
- 4 spring onion, chopped, whites and greens separated
- 4 eggs, whisked
- 1/2 tsp salt, or to taste
- 1 tsp sugar
- 1/2 tsp white pepper
- 1 tsp chicken bouillon powder

Clean and devein the prawns, then marinate with the oil, salt, white pepper and baking soda for 10 minutes. Pan-fry with a little oil for about 2 minutes until cooked through, then remove and set aside.

Heat 2 tbsp oil in the same pan over medium heat. Add the spring onion whites and cook for 30 seconds, then add the eggs and scramble until about 80% cooked. Add the rice, turn the heat to high and stir-fry for 2 minutes.

Season with the salt, sugar, white pepper and chicken bouillon powder and toss well. Taste and adjust if needed, then add the spring onion greens and prawns, reserving a few for serving.

To serve, arrange 3 prawns in a bowl, fill with fried rice and gently press down, then invert onto a plate.

💡 KEY POINTS:
- In this recipe, we’re swapping traditional Sake and Mirin for white wine and sugar in a certain conversion formula. As a Japanese home cook, I assure you it works perfectly to replicate the authentic taste. Only one simple rule you need to follow: 👉 Make sure to use a DRY and LOW-ACIDITY WINE (e.g. Pinot Gris). This is one of my favourite ways to pan-fry tofu until it’s beautifully golden and crispy, with all those little crunchy edges.

The trick is simple: gently smash the tofu to create more surface area, add a spoonful of flour (plain flour, corstarch, rice flour) to the hot oil, and then… leave the tofu alone.

Don’t flip it too early! Let the bottom turn properly golden and crispy first, then flip. This helps prevent the tofu from sticking to the pan and gives it that delicious crispy texture.

Serve it with a sweet and sour dipping sauce, or use it in one of my favourite Vietnamese noodle dishes: crispy tofu, rice noodles and a savoury soy sauce dressing. 🤤

L is for Lacto-Fermentation 

Ingredients:
* 100g citrus zest (lemon, lime, orange or a combination — avoid the white pith)
* 100g green chillies, roughly chopped
* 4g salt (2% of the combined weight of the zest and chillies)
Example: If your zest and chillies weigh 200g, you’ll need 4g salt.

Method:
Prep
1. Sterilise a glass jar and allow it to dry completely.
2. Finely zest your citrus, avoiding the white pith.
3. Roughly chop the green chillies, removing some seeds if you prefer less heat.

Blend
1. Weigh the combined citrus zest and chillies.
2. Add 2% salt by weight.
3. Blend into a coarse paste using a stick blender or food processor.
4. For a smoother texture, continue blending or finish with a mortar and pestle.

Ferment
1. Pack the paste tightly into the sterilised jar.
2. Press firmly to remove any trapped air pockets.
3. Cover loosely or use a fermentation lid.
4. Leave at room temperature for 2–5 days, tasting daily.
5. Once you’re happy with the flavour, refrigerate to slow fermentation.

Serve
1. Spoon over steak.
2. Stir through ramen or noodles.
3. Add to scrambled or fried eggs.
4. Toss through roasted vegetables.
5. Finish grilled seafood like scallops or prawns.
6. Mix into butter, mayonnaise or dressings for an instant flavour boost.

Storage
* Refrigerate for up to 6 months. The flavour will continue to develop over time.

Why does every Korean fridge seem to have a jar of these?

These Korean soy sauce pickles, called Jangajji (장아찌), are one of my favorite side dishes to keep in the fridge. They’re sweet, savory, tangy, crunchy, and somehow make every meal taste better.

I made this batch with cucumbers, Korean green peppers, asparagus, cabbage, and onions.

Recipe:

* 1 cup soy sauce
* 1 cup vinegar
* 1 cup sugar
* Whole black peppercorns
* Cucumbers
* Korean green peppers
* Asparagus
* Cabbage
* Onion

Directions:

* Wash and cut all vegetables.
* Place vegetables and peppercorns into a large container.
* Mix soy sauce, vinegar, and sugar in a 1:1:1 ratio.
* Pour the mixture over the vegetables.
* Let it sit overnight.
* The next day, remove only the liquid and bring it to a boil.
* Pour the hot liquid back over the vegetables.
* Let cool completely and refrigerate.

The result is a crisp, refreshing Korean side dish that’s perfect with rice, grilled meat, noodles, or any comforting meal.

A totally delicious salad with lots of textures and a lovely balance of acid, salt and sweetness. An easy salad to throw together if you’re having people over or equally as good on a weeknight. Enjoy! 

Recipe

1/3 cup pistachios chopped

🥦 ROMESCO BROCCOLI STEAKS 🌶️

The best way to cook broccoli is to burn it.

Charred broccoli florets served over puy lentils with a punchy romesco of roasted red peppers, hazelnuts and sundried tomatoes, and a herby gremolata drizzled over the top.

Serves 4
For the broccoli 
2 heads of broccoli

2 tsp garlic powder

½ tsp sea salt 
½ tsp black pepper

For the romesco 
250g roasted red peppers (jarred) 
2 tbsp sun-dried tomatoes 
100g blanched hazelnuts 
1 tsp smoked paprika 
Juice of ½ lemon 
1 tsp sherry vinegar

For the gremolata 
30g plant-based butter 
2 tbsp olive oil 
5g oregano 
¼ tsp salt

4️⃣ Melt the butter with the olive oil and oregano in a small pan until fragrant.

TOMATOES, HALLOUMI & BEANS. 

Make this for dinner tonight - just 15 minutes and it’s on the table. Grab some nice fresh bread and a glass of wine, and you’re good to go. 

Ingredients 
2 beefsteak tomatoes, thinly sliced 
1 banana shallot, thinly sliced 
2 garlic cloves, finely chopped 
3-4 sprigs of oregano, leaves picked 
1 packet of halloumi, sliced 
1 tsp of honey 
1 tsp of balsamic vinegar
1 jar (570g) of butterbeans
1/2 lemon zested, and juiced 
6g chives, finely chopped 
Olive oil, salt and black pepper 

Thinly slice the tomatoes, and cut the tops into bite-sized pieces (see video for reference). Spread the tomato slices on a plate or tray and sprinkle over some sea salt. Add a good drizzle of olive oil and gently flip the tomatoes to coat. Set aside. 
In a large frying pan over medium/high heat add 1/2 tbsp of olive oil. Add the shallot with a generous pinch of salt and cook gently until softened, about 5 minutes. Then add the garlic and offcut tomato pieces. Cook for 2-3 minutes before adding in the beans and letting it simmer for 5 minutes. Add the lemon zest, juice and some black pepper, then set aside. 
Clean out the pan and place it back on the heat. Add 1/2 tbsp olive oil, then add the halloumi slices, careful not to overcrowd the pan. Leave to char, about 2-3 minutes until golden brown, then flip and cook the other side. Drizzle over the honey and balsamic and finish with the oregano. Turn off the heat. 
Serve the beans on the base of a large platter, top with the tomato slices and their juices, and then scatter the halloumi on top. Sprinkle over the chopped chives, and enjoy right away, with some fresh bread to scoop everything up or pair it with some cooked grains (quinoa, freekeh, couscous, barley etc).

✅GUT & GLOW CRUNCH SALAD

If you want a healthy salad that actually tastes incredible and leaves you feeling refreshed, lighter, and satisfied… this is it. Its got all sorts of good stuff, super thinly sliced or diced so you get a little in each bite, plus its packed with gut friendly cabbage, hydrating cucumber, lots of fresh herbs and a creamy sesame ginger dressing that is honestly addictive.

You can add grilled chicken, steak, shrimp, salmon, tofu, or edamame to make it even higher protein.

INGREDIENTS:

For the salad:
1/2 green cabbage, thinly shredded
3-4oz arugula
1/2 English cucumber, thinly sliced
3-4 scallions, sliced
Handful of cilantro, chopped
Handful of fresh mint, chopped
Sesame seeds & peanuts (optional for crunch)

For the sesame ginger dressing:
1 to 1.5 inch chunk fresh ginger
3 garlic cloves
4-5 tbsp mayo
5 tbsp rice vinegar
1 tbsp sesame oil
1 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
Salt & pepper

Here’s how I made it:

1️⃣ Thinly shred the cabbage and add it to a large bowl along with the arugula, cucumber, scallions, cilantro, mint, sesame seeds, and chopped peanuts. The key is to ensure the cabbage is super thinly shredded (I used a mandolin) and finely dice the rest of the ingredients.

2️⃣ Add the ginger, garlic, mayo, rice vinegar, sesame oil, soy sauce or tamari, salt, and pepper to a blender or food processor. Blend until smooth and creamy.

3️⃣ Pour the dressing over the salad and toss really well until everything is coated.

4️⃣ Let it sit for 5-10 minutes so the cabbage softens slightly and absorbs all the flavor.

5️⃣ Add your favorite protein like grilled chicken, steak, shrimp, salmon, tofu, or edamame and enjoy.

This is my fennel, lentil, pea & spinach curry served with rice and soy yoghurt. 

RECIPE (serves 2)

INGREDIENTS 
• 1 tbsp oil
• 1 tsp black mustard seeds
• 8-10 curry leaves
• 1 medium fennel bulb, thinly sliced
• 2-3 garlic cloves
• 1 tsp grated ginger
• 1 tsp cumin
• 1/2 tsp turmeric
• 1 tsp coriander powder
• 1/4-1/2 tsp chilli powder
• 2 tbsp tomato puree
• 1 pouch/tin puy lentils (or beluga, green, or brown)
• 40g creamed coconut from a block
• 1/2 cup frozen peas
• 1 cup water 
• 2 large handfuls of spinach
• salt & pepper
• handful coriander, chopped
• juice from 1/2 a lemon, or to taste

Everything else: 
• 1 cup uncooked rice
• unsweetened soy yoghurt for serving

METHOD
1. Put your rice on to cook.
2. Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and temper the mustard seeds for 2 min before adding in the curry leaves for around 30 seconds. 
3. Add in the chopped fennel and cook for 5 min. 
4. Add in the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
5. Stir through the cumin, turmeric, ground coriander, and chilli powder, and tomato puree.
6. Add in the lentils, coconut, peas, and water. Mix, cover with a lid, and simmer for 4-5 min. 
7. Add in the spinach and cook for 2 more min, until wilted. 
8. Turn off the heat and stir through plenty or salt and pepper, and the lemon and coriander. 
9. Serve with the rice and yoghurt - enjoy!

Cod Grenobloise - Named after the landlocked city of Grenoble, the recipe was made to disguise what might be slightly older fish. (Not in this case!) 

60/40 Cure – Curing the Cod
25g table salt
15g caster sugar
-
Combine. Coat the fillet evenly and cure for 12 minutes. Rinse in cold water and pat dry thoroughly. Rest skin-side down on a tray lined with clean cloth, covering the flesh lightly with paper. For best results, refrigerate uncovered overnight to dry.
 
Cod Grenobloise
Serves two people
1 x 250g cod fillet, pin boned, trimmed and cured
100g butter
1 lemon, segmented (juice reserved)
20g capers
20g cornichons, diced
2 slices sourdough, small dice
20g flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped
20ml white wine
100ml fish stock (water or white wine if needed)
-
Portion the cod into 250g pieces or individual servings.
 
Melt 50g butter in a sauté pan and toast the diced sourdough over medium heat until golden; drain and reserve.
 
In the same pan, heat a thin layer of olive oil. Pat the cod dry and place flesh-side down into medium-hot oil. Do not move for 6–8 minutes; the fish will naturally release when ready. Lift out carefully and transfer skin-side down to an ovenproof dish. Add fish stock and dot with 25g of the butter. Braise at 160°C for 6–8 minutes, then rest.
 
Using the same pan, cook the remaining diced butter to noisette stage (golden brown with a nutty aroma), then remove from heat. Add reserved lemon juice and white wine (take care as it will spit) and shake to emulsify. Stir in capers, cornichons, lemon segments, croutons and parsley.
 
To serve, spoon warm cauliflower purée onto the plate. Remove the cod skin and place the fish on top. Spoon over the Grenobloise garnish and finish with olive oil.

COCONUT FISH CURRY 🥥🐟🔥 This is one of those low-effort, big-flavour dinners you’ll want on repeat.

Curry Paste
- 2 garlic cloves
- 1 thumb piece ginger
- 2 red chillies
- 1 bunch coriander, stalks
- 1 small onion, quartered
- 2 tsp ground turmeric
- 2 tsp ground cumin
- 2 - 3 tbsp water

Curry
- 550g firm fleshed fish (I’ve used salmon), cut into cubes
- 1 tsp mustard seeds
- 1 tbsp ghee (or butter)
- 1 x 400ml coconut milk
- 1 tbsp light soy sauce
- 1 lime, juiced
- 1/2 tbsp sugar

Toppings
- Chilli oil (optional)
- Fresh herbs (coriander, Thai basil etc.)
- Fried shallots

To make the curry paste, place all the ingredients into a food processor and blitz until smooth.

To make the curry, place a wok or pan over medium heat and add the mustard seeds. Toast until they pop then add ghee (or butter). Add the curry paste and turn up the heat frying off for 1 - 2 minutes, stirring continuously. Add coconut milk, stir well, put the lid on and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the fish cubes and poach on medium heat for 3 - 4 minutes, until just cooked through. Season with light soy sauce, lime juice and sugar. Balance seasoning as desired.

To serve, transfer to a dish and drizzle with chilli oil. Top with fresh herbs and fried shallots.

PARIS-STYLE POMMES ALLUMETTES 🥔🇫🇷

These matchstick fries “pommes allumettes” are ultra-thin, golden and lacy, bringing that irresistible French bistro crunch, the kind you’d find piled next to steak tartare in Paris. Surprisingly simple to make at home (no deep-frying needed!), they’re perfect tucked into a steak sandwich for extra crisp or served in a paper cone with garlic aioli for a fun apéro twist.

INGREDIENTS
4 large floury potatoes (Sebago or Russet)
1 tbsp neutral oil (sunflower, grapeseed or canola)
1 tsp cornflour (cornstarch)
½ tsp sea salt flakes, plus more to finish
Fine sea salt

METHOD
⭐️ Peel the potatoes and slice into 2–3mm thick rounds using a sharp knife. Stack and slice again into thin matchsticks, or use a julienne blade if you have one.
⭐️ Rinse the matchsticks in cold water, changing the water 2–3 times until it runs clear. Then soak for 15 minutes to draw out excess starch.
⭐️ Drain well, then dry thoroughly using a clean tea towel (don’t skip this wet potatoes won’t crisp).
⭐️ Heat oven to 220°C fan. Line 2 large trays with baking paper (avoid foil as it sticks).
⭐️ In a large bowl, toss the dried potatoes with oil, cornflour and salt. Mix with your hands to coat every piece evenly.
⭐️ Spread them in a single layer across the trays spacing them well.
⭐️ Bake for 15 mins. Flip the fries gently with a spatula and switch the trays (top to bottom). Bake for another 10 mins.
⭐️ Toss the fries and swap tray positions again (and rotate front to back), then bake 10-15 more mins or until golden and crisp.
⭐️ Serve hot with extra flaked salt or a pinch of fleur de sel. Excellent with aioli, Dijon, or whatever you’re dipping into.

My Go-To Mayo (that lasts) // Makes around 500ml

3 egg yolks
55g cider vinegar
6g salt
1 tbsp dijon mustard
400g neutral oil

1. Add everything to a tall, narrow container you have a lid for (meaning you can store it in the container in which you make it). 
2. Allow the mixture to stand for 5-10 minutes, until the egg yolks settle below the oil.
3. Dunk in a hand blender and push it to the bottom of the container. Blitz, keeping the blender firm to the bottom of the container, until the egg yolks become pale, then slowly move the blender up through the mix to emulsify the remaining oil into the mayonnaise.
4. Cover and store for up to 3 weeks in the fridge.

This is my go to recipe that you may have seen before. Very versatile, forgiving, and flat out delicious. It is 48-72 hours of total fermentation. Recipe and tips below!

For two-14 inch pizzas:

TIPS: 

-I Ball the dough the day before pizza. But you can ball 3-5 hours on the day of making pizza as well.

-I typically use @kingarthurbaking flours and Fleischmann INSTANT dry yeast.

-If you don’t like sugar, then don’t use it. I just like the coloring it provides. Or you can use honey or non diastatic malt powder.

-The goal of cold water is to manage the dough temperature throughout the process. Higher temp doughs during mixing can overproof faster.

-If using a mixer, I recommend adding crushed ice.

-When mixing, I always “under mix” so we can perform some stretch and folds to build gluten.

300 ml cold heavy cream

Meringue
Whip egg whites to soft peaks. Add sugar gradually until thick, glossy and completely smooth. Gently fold in cornstarch and vinegar.

Shape
Spoon small meringue mounds onto a drawn circle, making little wells and join into a wreath.

110°C (230°F)– 30 min

I have never tried freezing this, but never say never, to reheat, I’d add a splash of water & a touch more cream to the parsnips in the baking dish to keep things nice & saucy / creamy. 

4 large parsnips, peeled & core removed if very firm / woody, cut into wide batons 
3 garlic cloves, skin on
3 sprigs of thyme 
250mls cream 
2 tsp Dijon mustard 
Lots of grated nutmeg & black pepper 
Salt, to taste 
Large handful of hazelnuts, bashed roughly 

Boil parsnips, thyme & garlic in well salted water for around 4 mins, until pierce-able with skewer. Drain. Remove garlic from. Skins & finely mash / chop.

Arrange softened parsnips on baking dish. Sprinkle over the thyme too. 

In a small bowl mix Dijon, cream, garlic, nutmeg & lots of black pepper with pinch more salt & mix well. 

Pour cream mix over parsnips & bake in oven for around 30 mins until bubbling & getting nice colour. Add hazelnuts to the top & bake or flash under very hot grill until the top has good golden colour & the hazelnuts are nicely toasted.

I’ve made a variation of this salad for pretty much every other gathering for the past five years. People love it THAT much. 

I originally found the recipe in the @estelanyc cookbook and try a few new things every time I make it.
 You can serve it as an appetiser, or just as a great salad on the table. 

You’ll need:
* 3–4 heads of chicory/endive (red or white)
* 1 tangerine (or orange/mandarin)
* ~100g crystally, salty cheese (vintage cheddar, parmesan, comté)
* 1 small sprig rosemary
* A fist-sized piece of bread (sourdough or baguette)
* ~50g walnuts
* 1 garlic clove
* ½ fuyu persimmon or apple, cubed
* Olive oil, salt & pepper 
Do this:
* Tear the bread into irregular pieces and place on a baking tray with the walnuts. Finely grate over the garlic, add the rosemary, drizzle with olive oil and a pinch of salt. Toss and toast at 185°C for 10–15 min, until golden and crunchy. Cool slightly, then roughly chop.
* Mix the croutons with the crumbled cheese.
* Trim the chicory, separate the leaves, and place in a bowl. Grate over the tangerine zest, then squeeze in the juice. If very sweet, add a little lemon juice or vinegar.
* Just before serving, fold the persimmon or apple into the bread-cheese mix.
* Arrange chicory leaves on a plate and fill each with the crunchy mixture.
* Finish with pepper and flaky salt. Serve immediately.

CHILI CRISP BOK CHOY TOFU RICE 🌶️🥬🍚

If you’re spending $20 on grain bowls a few times a week, replace them with this. You’ll save $200/month!*

This rice cooker meal costs as little as $1 per serving (depending on how thrifty you are with your groceries) and takes 10 min of effort.

The general formula for this kind of rice cooker meal is:

1. 1 1/2 cups of rice (mix of brown and white)
2. 1 1/2 cups of liquid (water)
3. 1 - 2 cups of mix ins (bok choy and tofu)
4. 4 - 6 tbsp of sauce (chili crisp, brown sugar, soya sauce)

Add the rice and water to your rice cooker, then everything else on top. Cook!

Swapping the mix ins or sauce yields an entirely different meal. Once you internalize this formula, you’ll always know what to make.

Today’s version:

1 1/2 cups rice (brown + white mix)
1 3/4 cups water (more water because we used brown rice)
1 block tofu, cubed (about 300-400g)
2 bok choy
2 tbsp chili crisp
2 tbsp brown sugar
2 tbsp soy sauce

Add the rice + water, then tofu + bok choy, then drizzle sauce on top. Press cook (used the mixed setting if your rice cooker has one). Done!

Sticky soy glazed squash/pumpkin on the creamiest peanut lime sauce (and some steamy rice if that floats your boat)✨

The other day I had a Crown Prince pumpkin and it reignited my love of pumpkins/squashes. Can someone tell me why we are so obsessed with butternut squash in the UK?? It’s so average. This variety is nutty, sweet and rich and lends itself PERFECTLY to an umami, spicy glaze like this. Honestly I was in heaven and you will be to 🤝

RECIPE
½ Crown Prince pumpkin
Olive oil and salt

2 tbsp hoisin
2 tbsp sriracha
1 tbsp agave
1 tbsp soy
½ tbsp rice vinegar
1 tsp sesame oil
1 garlic clove, grated
1 inch piece peeled ginger, grated

100g smooth peanut butter
2 tbsp water (more if needed)
3 tbsp soy sauce
1 lime juice
2 tsp agave

To garnish:
1 tbsp white sesame seeds
1 tbsp black sesame seeds
1 tbsp chopped chives
Your favourite chilli crisp

1. Preheat the oven to 180 fan or 200C. Take half the squash and remove the seeds. Cut it into 4-5 thick wedges, leaving the skin on. Place the wedges onto a tray, drizzle with a splash of oil and salt then place into the oven to roast for 45 min.
2. Whisk together all the ingredients for the glaze. After 45 minutes baste the squash wedges with the sticky glaze. Repeat again after 10 mins then switch to grill to caramelise the sauce. Baste as many times as you want to get a nice thick coating of the sauce.
3. Quickly whisk together the ingredients for the peanut sauce then get ready to plate.
4. Whilst the squash is still on the tray, sprinkle over mixed sesame seeds and finely chopped chives.
5. Serve on a bed of the peanut sauce and dive in!

Vegan Dan Dan Noodles - Recipe below 

I love a quick and easy noodle recipe and this vegan version of the Chinese classic, dan dan noodles, is so delish. I have used crispy lentils and finely chopped mushrooms for the base to give you the right flavour and texture. A perfect noodle recipe for a quick and easy dinner x john 

Serves 2
1 x400g tin green lentils washed and drained
2 tbsp ground nut oil
300g chestnut mushrooms
1 tsp Sichuan pepper corns, lightly ground
1 dry chilli – crushed (2 if you like it hot)
1 inch ginger, minced
4 cloves garlic, minced
4 tbsp smith peanut butter
2 tbsp dark soy + 2 tsp
½ tbsp white wine vinegar
2 tsp chilli oil 
1 pack choi, cut into quarters 
180g medium egg noodles
2 spring onions, finely chopped

1. Preheat oven to 180c fan. Dry the lentils with kitchen paper and chuck them into a roasting tin. Add 1 tbsp of oil and toss together. Spread out and roast for 18-20 minutes or until crispy.
2. Blitz the mushrooms in a food processor.
3. Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a non-stick frying pan over a high heat. Add the Sichuan Pepper and chili. Stir-fry for 2-3 seconds until fragrant. Add the mushrooms, mix well and cook, stirring occasionally, for 12-15 minutes until you have cooked out the moisture and can hear a frying sound. Add the ginger and half the garlic and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add the 2 tsp of soy sauce and mix well.
4. Meanwhile, whisk the peanut butter together with 8 tbsp of just boiled water, a few tbsp at a time until smooth. Add the remaining soy sauce, vinegar, chilli oil and remaining garlic. Mix well. Divide between 2 serving bowls.
5. Cook the pak choi for 2 mins in pan of boiling water. Remove and add the noodles to the pan. Cook for 4-5 minutes or until al dente. Scoop out a little noodle water and drain. Divide the noodles between the two serving bowls and spoon 2 tbsp of noodle water over each. Add the pak choi.
7. Just before serving, toss the crispy lentils into the mushrooms. Spoon over the noodles and serve with spring onions on top and extra chilli oil.

Recipe: Crispy Shaved Tofu Salad
1. Shave 1 block of @sunrisesoyafoods extra firm tofu and mix with 1/4 cup of cornstarch, 1tsp each of: salt, onion powder, garlic powder, paprika and a pinch of cayenne.
2. In a separate bowl mix 2 cups of cooked, rinsed, and dried rice with a generous drizzle of oil, salt, onion powder, garlic powder and paprika.
3. On a greased pan, spread out the rice and tofu to a thin even layer (you can use 2 pans) and bake at 450F for 25-30mins until crispy.
4. While those cook, shred one whole English cucumber, a medium red onion and 1 large carrot, then press and drain out the liquid at the bottom(you can use this in stock). 
5. Mix together about 1/4 cup light mayo, and 2-3 Tbsp each of hot sauce and maple syrup, s&p to taste.
6. Once cooked and cooled for a couple mins, toss together the sauce, veggie shreds, crispy rice and tofu. 
7. Garnish with lots of toasted sesame seeds and crispy onions if you so choose!

Let’s elevate our day by making the best eggplant dish in the world — a Filipino classic called Tortang Talong 🍆🇵🇭

	•	Roast your eggplant until the skin blisters and turns soft
	•	Peel off the skin gently while keeping the head attached
	•	Mash the flesh flat with a fork
	•	Whisk an egg, pour it over the eggplant, and coat evenly
	•	Pan fry on medium heat until golden and crispy on both sides
	•	Serve with rice and your favorite sauce — sriracha, ketchup, or soy sauce all work perfectly 🍳

Two ingredient pasta dough in under 2 minutes, I have made this full dish in under 10 minutes after work before, it can be done! 

Hot Water Gnocchi
Gnocchi
00 pasta flour
boiling water
enough of each to form a tight dough.
-
Scale out flour into a large bowl. Boil your water. Add the water whilst piping hot to flour and stir to incorporate. Allow to hydrate and cool down for 2/3 minutes. Remove from the bowl and begin to work the dough until smooth and slightly elastic. Divide the dough into 4. Roll the dough section into a long strip and cut into equal thumbnail sizes balls. Using a gnocchi paddle or a grater, individually press the gnocchi on the board away from you. Store on a tray lined with semolina.
 
Cacio e Pepe – 2 servings
Hot water gnocchi (amount for 2 servings)
100g Parmesan, finely grated
100 g butter
2 tbsp black peppercorns, crushed (using a pan) or freshly ground with a peppermill
Salt for water, to taste
-
Blanch gnocchi - Cook the gnocchi in boiling, seasoned water for 2–3 minutes until they float. Reserve some of the starchy cooking water.
While the gnocchi cooks, crush the black peppercorns and lightly toast them in a dry sauté pan for 1–2 minutes to toast.
Ladle some of the reserved starchy water onto the toasted pepper. Add the hot gnocchi and reduce the water slightly around the gnocchi while tossing.
Remove from heat, emulsify in the butter, then gradually add Parmesan, tossing to create an emulsified sauce that coats the gnocchi.
Adjust seasoning with extra pepper if desired, and serve immediately finishing with freshly grated parmesan.

Creamy Buckwheat w Mushrooms 🍄‍🟫 🍂

Ingredients
- 100–150 g mushrooms
- 1 onion
- 1–2 tbsp butter
- 1 cup buckwheat
- 150–200 ml cream (10–20%) 
- 50–70 g cheese
- 2 cups hot water (or stock)
- Salt, to taste
- Fresh herbs, to garnish

Melt the butter in a pan and sauté the onion for a couple of minutes, then add the mushrooms and cook for about 10 minutes until softened. Stir in the buckwheat, mix well, then pour in the hot water or stock, cover with a lid, and cook on medium heat until the buckwheat is halfway done. Add the cream and continue cooking until tender. Sprinkle cheese over the top, let it melt, and finish with fresh herbs before serving.

EP. 2 Supergreen Pasta 

57g Protein | 557 Calories

Welcome to 50 30. Recipes with over 50g of protein that take less than 30 minutes to make.

INGREDIENTS FOR 2

240g Fusilli Pasta
 400g Cavolo Nero
 4 Garlic Cloves
 160g Cottage Cheese
 40g Light Soft Cheese
 50g Parmesan
 200g Cooked Shredded Chicken
 1 Lemon
 10g Parmesan (to serve)
 Pinch Dried Chilli Flakes
 Olive Oil
 Salt
 Black Pepper

METHOD
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil.
Strip the cavolo nero leaves from their stems and give them a rinse. Peel the garlic cloves.
Chuck the cavolo nero and garlic into the boiling water. Boil for 2 mins until tender, then drain and leave to cool slightly — or refresh in iced water if you want to lock in the colour.
Zest and juice the lemon. Grate the Parmesan.
Squeeze out any excess water from the cavolo nero, then chuck it into a blender with the garlic, cottage cheese, soft cheese, 50g grated Parmesan, a pinch of salt and pepper, and a couple of tablespoons of the blanching water. Blitz until smooth, adding more water if it’s not blending.
Bring the same pan of water back to the boil and cook the pasta following pack instructions until al dente.
Tip the drained pasta into a large bowl. Pour over the green sauce and toss until fully coated. Add the shredded chicken and toss again to warm it through — if it’s still a bit cold, pop the bowl over the hot saucepan to gently heat. If the sauce feels too loose, just keep tossing.

Gochujang Salmon Burgers with Quick Pickled Cucumber 🔥

For the burgers
	•	500g skinless salmon fillets (sorry @saffronfishco for blending your lovely salmon fillet 😆)
	•	80g tinned chickpeas (about ½ can), drained
	•	40g breadcrumbs (or oats)
	•	1 small red pepper, finely chopped
	•	1 garlic clove
	•	Small knob of fresh ginger (thumb-sized), peeled
	•	1½ tbsp gochujang
	•	1 tbsp soy sauce
	•	1 tsp sesame oil
	•	1 tbsp lime juice or rice vinegar
	•	1 egg
	•	Small handful fresh coriander or parsley (optional)
	•	Oil, for frying

For the quick pickled cucumber
	•	½ large cucumber, thinly sliced
	•	1 tbsp rice vinegar or white wine vinegar
	•	1 tsp sugar
	•	½ tsp salt
	•	1 tsp sesame oil
	•	Optional: pinch of chilli flakes or sesame seeds

To serve
	•	Brioche buns or lettuce wraps
	•	Gochujang mayo: 3 tbsp mayo + 1 tsp gochujang + squeeze of lime (or just yogurt)
	•	Optional extras: lettuce, pickled onion, sliced radish, rice, slaw etc.

1.	Make the burger mix: Add everything to a food processor - whole salmon fillets, chickpeas, breadcrumbs, red pepper, garlic, ginger, gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, lime juice, egg, and herbs (if using). Blitz until combined into a chunky paste.
	2.	Firm it up: Scoop the mix into a bowl and pop it in the freezer for 10 minutes to chill and firm up.
	3.	Pickle the cucumber: While the mix chills, combine vinegar, sugar, salt, and sesame oil in a small bowl or jar. Add sliced cucumber, toss well, and let sit to lightly pickle.
	4.	Shape and cook: Divide the salmon mixture into 4 patties. Heat a non-stick pan with a little oil, then fry the patties for 3–4 mins each side until golden and cooked through.
	5.	Serve: Add to toasted buns or wraps with gochujang mayo and plenty of pickled cucumber. Also great over rice bowls with crunchy veg.

Laid by hens who roam wide-open organic pastures, these @peteandgerrys eggs are as close to nature as breakfast gets. 

#eggs #breakfast #cooking #food

Ingredients (makes 4 servings) 

3 tablespoons room temperature butter 
1 teaspoon salt 
1/3 cup water 
12 large eggs 

1. Heat the oven to 325°F. Bring a pot of water to a boil. Grease an 8-inch square pan with butter. 
2. Blend together the salt, water and eggs until smooth. Place a mesh sieve over the square pan and pour the eggs in the pan. Scoop out the foam atop using a spoon. 
3. Place the square pan in a larger 9x13-inch pan. Fill the 9x13-inch pan with 1 inch of water. Tightly cover the 9x13-inch pan using an aluminum foil. 
4. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the eggs are giggly when shaken. Remove the pan from the oven and allow the eggs to rest at room temperature for 10 minutes. 
5. Divide into 4 and serve right away or store in the fridge or freezer. 
6. Serve in a sandwich with steamed squash, cheese and hot sauce for an irresistible seasonal breakfast.

🌱 Crispy Pepper Tofu Ochazuke 🍲

Got leftover rice? Make this. 

Ochazuke has been a Japanese staple for centuries, transforming day-old rice into a soothing, flavour-packed meal. 

Our version loads it up with crispy black pepper tofu, fluffy rice and a savoury miso broth, then piles on crunchy, fresh toppings for maximum texture and taste.

It’s light, nourishing and packed with plants. Save it for next time you need a warming meal x 

Serves: 2
Ingredients
For the crispy pepper tofu
* 1 block extra-firm smoked tofu
* 1 tbsp oil
* 1 tbsp soy sauce
* Generous pinch black pepper
For the ochazuke
* 300g short grain rice
* 600ml vegetable stock
* 1 tbsp white miso paste
* 1 tbsp soy sauce
* ½ tsp sesame oil
Toppings
* Sliced spring onions
* Pickled ginger
* Sliced nori
* Togarashi
* Edamame beans
* Fresh coriander leaves
Before you start Kettle | Small saucepan | Serving bowls
How to Make It
1️⃣ Crisp the tofu – Grate tofu on the coarse side of a cheese grater. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Fry tofu until golden and crispy. Remove from heat and stir in soy sauce + black pepper until coated and caramelised.
2️⃣ Make the broth – Heat stock until hot (not boiling). Whisk in miso paste, soy sauce and sesame oil until smooth. Keep warm.
3️⃣ Assemble the bowls – Spoon warm cooked rice into bowls. Arrange tofu, spring onions, edamame, pickled ginger and nori on top.
4️⃣ Pour & finish – Gently pour hot broth over each bowl. Top with coriander, a sprinkle of togarashi and an extra drizzle of sesame oil.

This is an apple cold brew tea made with Earl Grey tea.

Earl Grey tea is a flavored black tea and the flavor is bergamot, a citrus fruit, which gives this tea a very unique taste.

Since Earl Grey tea has citrus flavor already in the tea, I’m taking out the citrus part of my cold brew tea formula, which is 1 tea, plus 1 fruit plus 1 citrus plus 1 herb. I’m using Earl Grey as my tea, apple as my fruit, and mint as my herb. I find Fuji apples to be sweeter than other apples so that’s what I’m adding here.

Since everything gets strained, I cut up the entire apple, including the seeds and core. Cut the apple into small pieces so there’s more surface area for the fruit to infuse into the drink.

The tea, cut up apple, and torn mint goes into a container. Add cold or room temperature water and refrigerate for 12-24 hours. Strain out the solids and it’s ready to drink!

By the way, if you love Earl Grey tea, you need to cold brew it! It’s super crisp and the bergamot flavor really comes through.

PROTEIN PACKED PLATTERS: Glazed, Sticky Sweet Potatoes w/ Crispy Tofu + Peanut Sauce

Kicking off this new series with a bloomin’ good (and VE) one!

Serves 3–4.
▫️ 3 sweet potatoes, sliced lengthways ▫️ 1 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari) ▫️ 1½ tsp maple syrup ▫️ 1 block extra-firm tofu, cut into triangles ▫️ 1 small cucumber, shaved into ribbons ▫️ 100ml white vinegar ▫️ 200ml water ▫️ Spring onions + red chilli, to garnish

For the peanut sauce: ▫️ 2 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari if GF) ▫️ 1 garlic clove ▫️ 3 tbsp peanut butter ▫️ 2 tbsp plain yoghurt (I use high-protein) ▫️ 1 tbsp maple syrup ▫️ 1 inch fresh ginger ▫️ Juice of 1 lime

Method: 1. Steam the sweet pots: arrange in a deep baking tin, pour in a little water to cover the bottom, wrap tightly with foil and bake at 200°C fan for 20 mins.
2. Meanwhile, quick-pickle the cucumber: mix the vinegar, water and a pinch of salt, add the cucumber ribbons, toss and set aside.
3. Crisp the tofu: coat with oil, salt and pepper and air fry at 200°C for 10 mins. (Or bake.)
4. Glaze the potatoes: once steamed, uncover and drain any water. Mix the soy sauce and maple syrup, brush over the potatoes, then roast again. Pop the grill on for extra caramelisation.

🍜 THAI GREEN SPRING SOUP 🌱

spring is a time for vibrant bowls of soup SO we’re bringing it back with this THAI GREEN NOODLE creation, which hits that springtime spot to perfection 🌞

it’s a refreshing, zingy, yet comforting curried broth, packed with coconut milk, peanut butter and more for maximum flavour + texture 😍

topped with crunchy, crispy seasonal veg like asparagus, purple sprouting broccoli + oyster mushrooms. my full written recipe is below 👇 let me know if you give it a go!

INGREDIENTS (serves 2-3)

BROTH

30g fresh mint
30g fresh coriander
150g spinach
3 garlic cloves
1 small knob of fresh ginger
1 bunch spring onion (use whites for broth/greens for topping)
1 lime
1 tbsp each: peanut butter, soy sauce, agave syrup, mushroom stir fry sauce + miso paste (last two optional)
400ml coconut milk
1 litre vegetable stock

TOPPINGS

Carrot
Asparagus
(Purple sprouting) broccoli
Oyster mushrooms
Red chilli
Noodles of choice
Toasted sesame seeds
Crispy chilli oil 

METHOD

1. In a food processor/blender, peel + add the garlic, ginger, fresh herbs + spinach. Loosen with a splash of water if needed, then blitz. 
2. Add the peanut butter, soy, other seasonings if using, lime juice, agave + coconut milk, then blend again. Season to taste with salt + more agave if needed. 
3. Pour into a pot, then dissolve 1 veg stock cube in 1 litre boiling water. Add to the pot, bring to a boil then simmer on a low heat for 5-10 minutes. Add more boiling water for more broth, seasoning to adjust as is required. 
4. Prepare your toppings - I spiralized the carrots, blanched the asparagus + broccoli then sliced into spears & fried the oyster mushrooms until crisp.
5. Cook your noodles, then place in a bowl. Top with ladles of the green broth, then add your toppings. Finish with spring onions, chilli oil, sesame seeds + enjoy!

Creamy Mushroom & Miso Pasta✨

Say hello to your new weeknight dinner hero! 20g protein, 8g fibre, endless rich, creamy goodness – all coming together in just 15 minutes! So delicious, so easy, you’ll be making this one on repeat!

What You’ll Need:

- 300g dried pasta
- 600g chestnut mushrooms, sliced
- drizzle of olive oil
- 2 handfuls of spinach, finely sliced
- small bunch of chives
- several grinds of freshly ground black pepper
- 20g dried porcini mushrooms
- 2 cloves garlic
- 300g silken tofu
- 2 tablespoons brown rice miso paste
- ½ lemons

How To Make It: 

1. Place the dried mushrooms in a bowl and cover with 150ml boiling water. Leave to soak for 10 minutes.
2. Next, put the pasta on to cook according to the instructions on the pack.
3. While the pasta cooks, place a frying pan over medium-high heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Once warm, add the sliced chestnut mushrooms and a pinch of salt. Cook for 5–10 minutes, until tender.
4. Once the dried mushrooms have been soaking for the correct amount of time, place them in a blender, along with their soaking liquid and the rest of the sauce ingredients. Blend until smooth sauce forms, season to taste.
5. Stir the drained pasta, the sauce, the chopped spinach, and the chives into the mushroom pan, cook together for a minute or so, until the spinach has wilted, adding a little of the reserved pasta water if needed. Serve with sea salt and lots of black pepper.

Crispy Rice Omelette recipe 🍚 5 minutes is all it takes to turn your leftover rice into this tasty snack!

This 5-minute Crispy Rice Omelette is a perfect way to use up any leftover rice in the fridge. Inspired by a recipe by @the_foodiediaries - this version uses a quick Gochujang Butter to fry the rice and gives it a beautiful sweet x spicy flavour. Load it up with whatever veg you want and you've got yourself a quick and delicious meal 😋 

Recipe 👇 

Ingredients
2/3 cup of leftover rice
2 eggs (whisked together)
1 Tbsp gochujang
1 Tbsp butter
1-2 Tbsp oil of choice
1/4 cup veg and herbs of choice - I used corn, spring onion greens and coriander

Method
1) Break up the leftover rice with your hands to remove any clumps. Make the gochujang butter by mixing together the gochujang and butter. 
2) Heat frying pan over medium high heat and add the oil. Add the rice and fry for about 1 minute, then add the gochujang butter and coat the rice. Press the rice across the bottom of the pan to make a circle and leave to fry for 1-2 minutes, then pour the whisked eggs over. Cover and cook for about 1 minute until the egg is just starting to set, then uncover and sprinkle over the veg/herbs of choice.
3) Fry uncovered for a further minute then use a spatula to release the sides/bottom of the rice (the rice should be crispy and pulling away from the pan). In one motion fold the rice over itself, plate up and serve!

Cacio e Pepe chickpeas with Balsamic Tofu 

A reminder that you don’t have to be vegan, or 100% plant-based, plant forward or even plant predominant to gain the benefits associated with eating more plant protein. Try switching an omnivorous meal with this and see what you think.

Send to your local friendly carnivore! 😉

Ingredients 
1 medium or 2 small leeks, cut into fine half moons, washed.
4 cloves garlic, grated 
About 10-12 turns of freshly cracked black pepper 
700g chickpeas, from a jar or 2 x 400g cans. Keep the water, or rinse and add 100ml. 
For the creamy sauce: 200g silken tofu, 100g cashew nuts, soaked in boiling water for 10 mins, 4 tbsp nooch, 1 tsp marmite (or sub miso paste) + a splash of water for blending 
280g extra firm tofu 
4 tsp cornstarch 
Pinch of sea salt 
Tofu marinade: 1.5 tbsp Dijon mustard, 2 tbsp balsamic vinegar, 1.5 tbsp tamari 

To serve: fresh herbs, olive oil

Method:

In a blender cup, whizz the silken tofu, soaked cashew nuts, nooch, marmite and splash of water. Set aside.

Fry the leeks on low/medium in olive oil with a pinch of salt for 5 mins. Add the garlic and black pepper, fry 2 mins more. Add the chickpeas + their water (or drain and add a splash of water, add a little salt too!). Heat through, then leave to stand whilst you make the tofu. 

Squeeze out any excess liquid, then roughly tear the chunks and add to a mixing bowl with the cornstarch and salt. Toss well, then fry off in olive oil in a non-stick pan until it goes a shade of yellow. Whisk the tamari, mustard and balsamic, add that to the tofu, then turn down the heat and stir until it’s mostly absorbed, about 3-5 mins. 

Back to the chickpeas, turn the heat back on, warm through, then pour over the creamy sauce from earlier, season to taste, and gently heat for 2-3 mins, then serve with the tofu on top.

Garlic Butter Halloumi Schnitzel 
Did you know that if you soak halloumi in boiling water, you can roll it out and make a schnitzel?!

I just covered these in breadcrumbs and fried it so it was thin and crispy and honestly, add some chips and it is just the BEST weekend dinner!

I drizzled mine in this storecupboard version of garlic butter, using dried parsley and garlic paste, so it could NOT be easier - you can even cook them in the airfryer!

I have written up the recipe below, let me know if you're going to give it a try! A x

Makes 4 halloumi steaks 

2 blocks of halloumi (cut carefully in half lengthways)
1 large egg beaten
A large handful of fresh or panko breadcrumbs
Oil for frying
60g butter
1 tsp garlic paste
1 tsp dried parsley

Place the halloumi quarters in boiling water and leave to soak for 15 minutes.
Carefully lift them from the pan (one at a time, leave the rest in while you bread the halloumi) and place them on a double sheet of kitchen roll. 
Place more kitchen roll on top of the halloumi and gently roll it out. When it's thin and double the size leave it to cool completely before moving.
Roll in flour until coated then tap off excess
Dip it in beaten egg, then place on a plate of breadcrumbs, making sure each side is covered.
Repeat with the rest of the halloumi.
Fry for a couple of minutes on each side until crisp and golden brown.
Place the butter, parsley and garlic paste in a microwave safe bowl. Season and microwave until the butter has melted. 
Stir and pour over the crispy halloumi
Serve immediately

brothy beans formula (+ how to cook dried beans) 🫘 🍲 🥬 some researchers even call them the “ultimate longevity food”! 

first, a few quick myths to bust: 
-soaking them overnight will reduce their cook time (like 1-2hrs compared to 2-3hrs) but it’s not necessary 
-salting your beans when they start simmering will not make them tough (it has literally never happened to me and I make this minimum monthly) 
-foods with lectins (like beans and nightshades) are not bad for you. and soaking/simmering/cooking deactivates lectins.  lots to say here, so if you want more info/another video, let me know 

ok, on to the brothy beans formula: 
-brown wedges of onions/shallots, garlic and half a (deseeded) lemon until lightly browned. 
-add desired spices and herbs, and stir until fragrant (1-2 minutes) 
-add your beans, water and parm rind (if using). in general, for every 1 cup of beans I add about 4-6 cups of water to start. you want all the beans to stay submerged so don’t be afraid to add more as they cook. 
-simmer for a minimum (!!) of 2 hours. to see if they’re done, taste a bean. it should be soft and creamy without any notable crunch. 
-remove the parm rind and lemon. 

serve what you want to eat now (with wilted greens and toast/grilled cheese perhaps?) and save the rest!

If you forget to eat protein sometimes like me, then consider adding cooked chickpeas to your rice!

I usually do 2:1 part rice to chickpeas. Sometimes more, sometimes less. I think this should work with any cooked bean. 

Red or brown lentils work too, but I like using cooked chickpeas as they do not interfere with the cooking process of the rice. If you use uncooked beans then they will soak up water as part of their cooking, which means you’d need to add more water overall. 

I hope this little tip helps! Follow @friendlyveg_ for more 🫶

JAPANESE SPINACH SESAME SALAD🌱 [Recipe👇🏼] 
Servings: 2

One of my favourite appetizers - goma-ae! Super easy and nutrient packed. The dressing can be made while the spinach cools down! 

Ingredients:
- 2 tbsp toasted sesame seeds (into a paste, a blender is good to use) 
- 2 tbsp low sodium tamari or soy sauce (I’m using @sanjtamari)
- 1 tbsp mirin
- 1 tsp sugar (I subbed honey, but it imparts a different flavour)
- 1 tsp salt

Method:
Dressing
- add toasted sesame seeds into a mortar, and grind until halfway ground. 
- add tamari, mirin, money and mix well.
optional:
-can add all sauce ingredients in to a blender and mix well.

Spinach:
- add water and a tsp salt to a medium pot and boil
- wash spinach well. Mature spinach can collect lots of dirt in between the leaves
- when water is boiling, arrange the spinach so all stems are bunched together, and insert only the stalks into the boiling water. Hold it hear for about 1-2 minutes (thicker the stalks, longer)
- after 1 minute, dunk the rest of the spinach leaves under water and cook for another 1-2 minutes.
- strain and immediately add to ice water bath to cool down and stop the cooking process.
- once cooled, squeeze out excess water, and cut the spinach into 1.5-2” chunks
- add to a bowl, add sesame dressing mix well and can leave in fridge. Remove about 30 minutes before serving to warm up to room temp

Janssons Frestelse, “Janssons Temptation” is a quintessential Swedish Christmas dish.

It was first described in 1928 and was originally a midnight meal after parties to still the hunger of drunk guests. 

It’s basically a potato gratin. The main differences is that the potato is cut into sticks and that it’s layered with cured sprats “ansjovis”. The name might make you think that it’s anchovies, but ansjovis are actually cured sprats. They remind me a little bit of matjes herring. They have a briney, somewhat sweet, spiced flavour because they are cured with spices such as cinnamon, cloves, black pepper, cardamom and sandalwood. 

While only real ansjovis will give you the “right” flavour, this dish will still be delicious with substitutions. You could go for regular salted anchovies (use a bit less as they are saltier) or capers for a vegetarian alternative. Or, you could even leave it out entirely. 

Anyway here’s how you can make:

1.2kg waxy potatoes
500ml cream 
100ml milk 
1 can of sprats (sub with anchovies or capers)
2 onions
4 tablespoons butter
Breadcrumbs
Salt & Pepper

1. Preheat your oven at 200c.
2. Peel the onions and slice thinly. Heat a large skillet on medium with 1 tablespoon butter. Add the onions, season with salt and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring every few minutes to avoid burning. The onions are done when they are soft and starting to caramelise (they don’t have to be fully caramelised though)
3. Peel the potatoes and cut them into skinny fries shaped sticks. 
4. Grease a 28x20cm baking dish (or about 13x9 inch) with butter. 
5. Layer potatoes, onions and sprats in the baking dish. Season with salt and pepper in every layer, ensuring that the first and last layer are potatoes. Pour over the cream. 
6.  Finish with a few pats of butter and an even layer of breadcrumbs
7. Bake in the bottom of the oven at about 1 hour. If it starts getting too dark you may want to cover it with foil. #swedishfood #christmasfood #comfortfood

I have been wanting to make a mushroom bourguignon for so long, and loved the idea of using baby button mushrooms for it. 
 I was actually surprised of how well this turned out. It’s unbelievably rich (even though it’s vegetarian!) and I’d like to think that my imaginary grandfather would be proud of me. 

Ingredients:
* 400g baby mushrooms
* 12 small chantenay carrots (or 2 large carrots, chopped)
* 10 small shallots or pearl onions, peeled
* ½ onion, finely minced
* 1 celery stalk, finely minced
* 5 garlic cloves, finely minced
* A few sprigs of fresh thyme
* 175ml red wine
* 500ml stock (beef stock for the richest flavor, or mushroom stock for vegetarian)
* 2 tbsp tomato paste
* 2 tbsp chipotle in adobo sauce (optional, for smoky heat)
* 2 heaping tbsp all-purpose flour
* 50g butter
* Olive oil (for frying) 
Instructions:
 * Cut the stems off the mushrooms. Mince the stems finely, and keep the mushroom heads whole.
 * Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large, very hot pan. Add the mushroom heads and cook until browned on one side (about 80% cooked). Remove and set aside.
 * In the same pan, melt the butter and stir in the flour. Cook, stirring constantly, until the mixture turns a caramel-brown color, creating a dark, rich roux.
 * Add the minced onion, celery, and minced mushroom stems to the pan. Sauté for a few minutes until softened.
 * Add the garlic and tomato paste, cooking for 2-3 minutes to deepen the flavors.
 * Pour in the red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Let it reduce for about a minute.
 * Add the stock, thyme sprigs, and chipotle in adobo sauce (if using). Stir well.
 * Add the carrots and shallots or pearl onions. Simmer for 5-10 minutes, or until the carrots are just fork-tender but still have a slight bite.
 * Return the sautéed mushroom heads to the pan and cook for another 1-2 minutes to warm through and let flavors meld.
 * Serve hot with a buttery potato purée and a sprinkle of fresh chives. Enjoy!

It’s that time of year again! The Smoked Salmon Savoury Dutch Baby.

4 eggs
180g milk
90g plain flour
1/4 tsp salt
40g butter
20g parmesan cheese
15g fresh parsley, dill & tarragon
1 garlic clove

To serve

200g smoked salmon
50g crème fraîche
2 tsp fresh dill
1 tbsp lemon juice
1 tsp lemon zest
1/4 tsp salt

Preheat your oven to 230°C (445°F) and place your cast iron pan on the middle shelf. Make sure there’s enough space above it for your Dutch Baby to expand.
In a stick blender jug add the eggs, flour, milk & salt. Blend until smooth and aerated. This can also be done in a stand up blender.
Leave the mixture to stand whilst the oven comes up to temperature. The closer the mix is to room temp, the better rise you’ll get in the finished product.
Grate the parmesan, chop the herbs fine and mince the garlic. Transfer to a bowl. I like to add a pinch of salt to this mixture also.
When you’re ready to go, remove the pan from the oven and add the butter. Let it bubble and melt down completely. Then pour your batter mix into the pan.
Scatter the cheese and herb mix over the top and return to the oven for 15 to 20 minutes. Do not open the oven during this time.
To serve

In a bowl mix the crème fraîche, chopped dill, lemon juice, lemon zest and salt.
Arrange the smoked salmon in the bottom of the Dutch Baby and spoon over the dill crème fraîche.

For the printable recipe go to eatlikeanadult.com and search ‘Dutch baby’. Or just Google ‘eat like an adult smoked salmon Dutch baby’.

A few notes:

- Get the batter to room temperature before cooking to get a good rise.
- That is an obscene amount of butter :) You don’t really *need* that much (the recipe on my site is correct) but it’s only Christmas once!
- Yes, it’s one pan because I didn’t include the blender jug.
- Isn’t this just a huge Yorkshire pudding? Call it whatever makes you happy. 
- What’s Dutch about it? Nothing. The name comes from an American misunderstanding of ‘Deutsche’ because it’s based on a German pancake.
- The pan doesn’t have to be cast iron, just one that can go in the oven. That includes similar sized and shape cake tins.
- How does it rise without yeast? Steam!

SPROUT KRAUT WITH MAPLE & CHILLI 📌

INGREDIENTS

400g Brussels sprouts
8g sea salt
1 tbsp chilli flakes
1 tbsp mustard seeds
2 tbsp maple syrup
Water to submerge the kraut

METHOD

1. Slice the sprouts finely, so they’re almost shredded.

2. In a large bowl, add the salt, chilli and mustard seeds and massage for about 5 minutes until they start releasing their liquids.

3. Pack all the sprouts into a clean glass jar (quart-size or larger), leaving about 1-2 inches of space at the top.

4. Pour over the water and add your maple syrup too. Use a fermentation weight or a clean, small glass to keep the sprouts submerged under the brine, as this prevents exposure to air (which can cause mould).

5. Leave the jar to ferment at room temperature, checking daily to ensure they stay submerged. If any scum or foam forms, skim it off with a clean spoon.

6. After 3 days, begin tasting the sprouts. We recommend fermenting for 5-7 days but as soon as they reach your preferred level of tanginess, transfer the jar to the fridge to slow down the fermentation process. Enjoy!

Cauliflower & Sweet Potato Cheese Bake - nourishing comfort food made simple 💫

You simply roast sweet potato and cauliflower until golden and tender, then bake with butter beans and kale in a rich, creamy cashew sauce. Packed with veggies, easy to prep ahead, and incredibly satisfying, it’s a weeknight winner.

For the sauce:  150g cashews 400ml hot vegetable stock 4 tablespoons nutritional yeast 200ml oat milk 2 tablespoons Dijon mustard ½ lemons, zested & juiced 
For the cauliflower bake:  1kg cauliflower, cut into florets 400g sweet potatoes, peeled & cut into 2cm chunks 1 onion, halved & finely sliced 2 large cloves garlic, thinly sliced
3 tablespoons olive oil 1 x 400g tin butter beans, drained & rinsed 2 large handfuls of kale 
Here’s how to make it:

1. Preheat the oven to 200°C fan / 425°F. Pour the cashews and hot stock into a heat-proof bowl; set aside to soften.
2. Place the cauliflower, sweet potato, onion, garlic and 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large casserole dish, season generously and toss together. Bake for 35–40 minutes until tender and golden.
3. Tip the cashews and stock into a high-speed blender, followed by the oat milk, nutritional yeast, mustard, lemon zest and juice, some salt and plenty of black pepper; blitz until smooth.
4. Pour over the sauce, add the butter beans, kale and mix everything together. Drizzle a little olive oil over the top (optional).
5. Bake for 15—20 minutes, until bubbling and golden. Delicious served with steamed greens.

A little tip to change your life, add a tin of white beans to your pesto 👌 Makes it extra creamy and instantly turns a staple meal into something extra nutritious and packed with protein, especially when you add peas too. This works perfectly with any pasta, today I’m making it with orzo (my kids love orzo so we eat it a lot) ✨ Here’s how to make it:

Serves 4:
- 400g orzo or other short pasta 
- 400g frozen peas
- 100g pine nuts, roasted 
- 50g basil, leaves and stalks roughly chopped
- 2 garlic cloves, finely chopped
- 100ml extra virgin olive oil
- 1× 400g tin of cannellini or butter beans, drained and rinsed
- 1 tablespoon nutritional yeast 
- squeeze of lemon 
- sea salt and black pepper

1. Bring a large saucepan of well salted water to the boil. Add the orzo and boil for 5 minutes then add the peas and boil for another 2–3 minutes, until the orzo is tender and the peas are cooked through.

2. While the pasta is cooking, toast the pine nuts in a dry frying pan over a high heat for a minute or so, until golden. Stir and toss them around to prevent them burning.

3. Place 3/4 of the toasted pine nuts into a blender or processor with all the basil, garlic, olive oil, beans and nutritional yeast and blitz for a couple of minutes until blended to a thick pesto.

4. Drain the pasta and peas and reserve about 200ml of the cooking water. Return the cooked pasta and peas to the saucepan.

5. Pour the pasta water slowly into the food processor with the motor running until you have a sauce – you may not need all of the water, so add it slowly.

6. Pour the sauce over the orzo and peas and mix well. Serve immediately with a squeeze of lemon and a scattering of toasted pine nuts

MISO-GLAZED HONEYNUT SQUASH 

▪️4 honeynut squash

▪️Kosher salt & fresh black pepper
▪️2 TBSP white miso, at room temp 
▪️1 ½ TBSP apple cider vinegar
▪️1 TBSP soy sauce
▪️1 heaping TBSP organic brown sugar

BALSAMIC GLAZED LEEKS + MUHAMMARA 🌶️

leeks might be one of my favourite vegetables. here, I’ve served them as the star of the show. seared, glazed + dipped in muhammara, a delicious roasted red pepper dip. 

ad | to prepare the leeks + dip, I used a variety of my favourite @odysea_ltd oils, vinegars + seasonings. good quality extra virgin olive oil, balsamic vinegar, harissa, peppers + more 🔥

served best as a sharing plate with salad + flatbreads, I’ve written my full recipe for you in the caption below. so enjoy + let me know if you give it a go 👇

INGREDIENTS (serves 4 as a side)

2 leeks
4 tbsp Odysea balsamic vinegar

1 jar Odysea roasted peppers 
1 garlic clove
1 tsp smoked paprika
1 tsp ground cumin
1 tsp Odysea pomegranate harissa
1 tsp tomato purée
75g toasted walnuts
2 tbsp toasted breadcrumbs
2 tbsp Odysea pommegranate molasses
1 lemon

1/2 red chilli
2 tbsp fresh parsley
1 tsp agave (optional)
Odysea extra virgin olive oil
Salt
Pepper

TO SERVE: salad + (flat)breads

METHOD

1. To make the muhammara, either roast your own peppers + peel off the skin, or simply combine jarred peppers in a food processor with the garlic, paprika, cumin, harissa, tomato purée, walnuts, breadcrumbs, molasses + lemon juice. Blitz to combine - you want a chunky but smooth texture. 
2. Season with salt + pepper, adjusting to taste + streaming in 1-2 tbsp olive oil to help emulsify. 
3. Slice the leeks into chunky rounds, season with salt + pepper. 
4. Warm a good glug of olive oil in a frying pan on a medium high heat. Add the leeks + sear for 5 minutes on each side, or until golden brown. Flip + repeat, then deglaze the pan with 1-2 tbsp balsamic vinegar. Finish off on a baking tray in the oven at 180 celsius for 5-10 mins. 
5. For the dressing, simply whisk 3 tbsp evo with 2 tbsp balsamic, 1/2 a chopped red chilli, chopped parsley + a splash of sweetener if using. Season to taste with salt + pepper. 
6. To serve, spoon the muhammara in the centre of a plate. Place the leeks on top, then dress generously with the vinaigrette. Serve with salad + bread then enjoy!

Comforting Salmon Soup in Under 30 Minutes!
 I hadn’t made this in ages, and honestly, I was blown away by how comforting and delicious it is—especially considering how EASY it is to make

Growing up, my mom made her own version regularly—sometimes with cod, sometimes with prawns. She even sent me a picture of her 1980s Finnish cookbook Keittotaito, where the original recipe calls for milk instead of cream. Back then, cream was considered a luxury too extravagant for soup. Luckily for us, times have changed! I’ve added cream and a touch of lemon to brighten it up.

Here’s what you’ll need for 2 generous portions. 
* 400g salmon, cut into chunks (or your favorite fish!)
* 250g potatoes, bite-sized (baby potatoes are my favorite)
* 1 piece leek, sliced
* 1 carrot, cut into chunks
* 100ml cream
* 500ml water
* 1 fish broth cube
* 1 bunch of dill, chopped
* 1 lemon, zested and juiced
* 1 tsp corn starch 
Steps: 1️⃣ Heat a tablespoon of olive oil in a large pot. Sauté the leeks with a pinch of salt for 2-3 minutes. 2️⃣ Add the potatoes, carrots, water, and broth cube. Simmer for about 10 minutes, or until the veggies are almost tender. 3️⃣ Gently stir in the salmon, lemon zest, dill, and cream. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes, until the fish is perfectly cooked. 4️⃣ Mix corn starch with 1 tablespoon of hot water, then stir it into the soup to thicken slightly. Season with salt and pepper to taste. 5️⃣ Ladle into bowls, squeeze in fresh lemon juice, and enjoy!

2-3 cloves Garlic, finely minced

sesame oil, for greasing

1 tbsp Sugar

METHOD 
Soak rice and mushrooms the night before (cold water) - soak extra mushrooms (5-6 pieces if you want to line/crown your bowls with a mushroom). When @waitrose asked me to share my favorite comfort food, I immediately thought of laxpudding. My first girlfriend’s Swedish grandmother made it for me ten years ago, and it’s been a staple ever since—a cozy, comforting dish that always feels like a hug.

With just a handful of ingredients, here’s how to make it: 
Ingredients:
* 800g waxy potatoes
* 1 onion
* 300ml cream
* 100ml milk
* 3 eggs
* 240g smoked salmon
* 100g butter
* 1 bunch of fresh dill, minced
Method:
1. Peel the potatoes and boil in salted water until fork-tender. Let cool, then slice.
2. Thinly slice the onion and cook in the butter until soft, reserving the melted butter.
3. Whisk together cream, milk, and eggs, seasoning with salt and pepper.
4. Layer the sliced potatoes, smoked salmon, cooked onions, and fresh dill in a baking dish, pouring a bit of the cream mixture between each layer. Finish with a final layer of the cream mixture on top.
5. Bake at 175°C for about 30 minutes, until the top is golden and bubbly.
6. Drizzle with the reserved melted butter and garnish with a sprinkle of fresh dill.
I love serving it with a simple green salad tossed in lemon juice. Enjoy!

Fermented Pickled Cucumbers Recipe 
Ingredients: 
• 10 cucumbers (small to medium size, firm and fresh) 
• 4 cups water (non-chlorinated) - 900g 
• 2 tablespoons sea salt or kosher salt (non-iodized) - 30g 
• 3 garlic cloves, peeled and halved

Vinegar Pickled Cucumbers Recipe 
Ingredients: 
• 10 cucumbers (small to medium size, firm and fresh) 
• 2 1/2 cups water 
• 1 1/2 cups white vinegar 
• 4 TBSP Salt - 60g 
• 2 TBSP sugar - 30g 
• 3 garlic cloves, peeled and halved 
• 2 sprigs of Fresh dill 
• 1/2 tsp red chili flakes 
• 1/2 tsp mustard seeds 

Preparing Brine (pickling solution) 
- Fermentation brine is simply water and 2-5% Salt (relative to weight of water). Go with 3% sea salt and stir till the salt is fully dissolved. 
- Vinegar brine, bring the salt and sugar to a simmer to ensure they are fully dissolved, and let the solution cool down before pouring into the jar for maximum crispness. 

Pickling and storage 
- My ideal time is 1 week pickling on the shelf and then store in the fridge 
- Fermented pickles need to remain in the fridge all the time after the first week. 
- Vinegar pickles can remain on the shelf till they are opened, then best stored in the fridge. 

Preparing Jars 
- It is critical that you sanitize the jars used for fermentation. My preferred way is to boil in shallow water for 12 minutes. 
- For vinegar pickling, a good clean jar will do without the need for sanitization (for home use) 

Usage 
- I find fermented pickles to be best for Arabic dishes, shawarma, Falafel ... 
- And Vinegar pickles with burgers, crispy chicken..

SMASHED POTATO SALAD 🥔

Welcome back to SALAD SEASON, where I show you how to make the best salads in town. 

For EPISODE 10, we’ve made a CRISPY SMASHED POTATO SALAD. Now I love the classic potato salad, but smashing then roasting until crispy + golden takes things to the next level. Especially as we move into the autumn months 🍂

My full recipe can be found below - enjoy! And let me know if you give it a go 👇

* shout out to @makemiameal_ from @twistedgreen for recipe inspo - the smashed potato queen 🥔👸*

INGREDIENTS (serves 4 as side)

750g baby new potatoes
Seasoning mix: 1tbsp each chicken + piri piri seasoning (I use @cornishseasalt or use smoked paprika + garlic powder)
3 tbsp mayo (I use @hellmannsuk plant-based)
3 tbsp greek style yoghurt (I use @coconutcollab)
1 lemon
1 garlic clove
2 tbsp each: pickled gherkins, cucumber, red onion, chives + dill
Salt
Pepper
Olive oil

METHOD

1. Place your potatoes in a pot of cold, salted water. Bring to the boil, then simmer until fork tender (25-30 minutes). Meanwhile, pre-heat your oven to 200 degrees celcius. 
2. Whilst the potatoes boil, make the dressing. In a mixing bowl, combine mayo, yoghurt, lemon juice + garlic. Then finely dice the gherkins, cucumber, onion, chives + dill, adding to the bowl. Mix well to combine, then season to taste with salt + pepper. Leave to sit in the fridge until serving. 
3. Once the potatoes are fork tender, allow to steam dry completely. Then, on a large lined baking tray, place + flatten the potatoes with the bottom of a glass - being careful not to overcrowd. 
4. Sprinkle with your seasonings of choice, then drizzle generously with olive oil. Roast for 30-45 minutes, turning half-way, until completely crisp + golden. You may need to add a splash more oil if required. You could also probably do this in an airfryer - but might require some experimentation!
5. Allow the potatoes to cool once cooked, then in a large mixing bowl spoon 1/2 the dressing. Pour in the potatoes, then mix carefully to fully coat. Add more dressing as required, then I like to finish with more fresh herbs. Serve as a side, or simply enjoy!

🌱 1 large handful of fresh parsley, finely chopped
🌱 1/4 red onion, finely chopped
🌱 crusty bread, to serve (optional)

Preheat the oven to 180°C fan / 400°F. Remove the leaves from the cauliflower and slice the head down the middle. Slice a 2cm (0.8”) thick steak from each half of the head so you’re left with two cauliflower steaks. Save any leftover cauliflower for another recipe.

Transfer the steaks to a baking tray. Drizzle both sides with olive oil and season with salt and pepper, then bake for 15 minutes.

Combine the sliced garlic and a small drizzle of olive oil in a bowl. Remove the cauliflower from the oven, flip over the steaks, then spoon the garlic and oil over the top of the cauliflower steaks. Return the cauliflower to the oven for another 15 minutes or until tender.

Meanwhile, add the roasted red peppers, blanched almonds, tomato puree, juice from half of the lemon and small pinches of salt and pepper to a fast-powered blender. Blend until silky smooth, then set aside.

Next, add the parsley and red onion to a bowl, along with the juice from the remaining half of lemon and small pinches of salt and pepper. Mix, then stir in enough olive oil until the dressing runs smoothly off a spoon, then set aside.

To serve, spoon the romesco sauce on plates, then top with the cauliflower steaks and drizzle over the parsley dressing. We also love to scoop up the sauce with crusty bread! Enjoy.
