Cheesy root vegetable Gratin. 

I love the subtly sweet and earthy flavors of this combination of root vegetables mixed together with the savory and salty shredded gruyère cheese, garlic, thyme, and heavy cream.

✅ Grease baking dish with butter.
✅Slice sweet potato,  gold potato and purple potato into very thin rounds (using a mandoline is easiest).
✅The aluminum foil should be tightly wrapped around the baking dish to allow the dish to steam a little and for the vegetables to get tender before uncovering it.
✅Keeping the slices as uniform in thickness as possible will greatly help even cooking throughout the gratin.
✅Using a mandoline will not only ensure even thickness, but will also reduce the prep time. If you don’t have a mandoline a very sharp knife is the next best thing I recommend
✅Covering this dish in the beginning will allow the vegetables to soften without drying the dish out. Once the vegetables get to a good point, uncovering them will allow the top of the gratin brown and crisp up, while allowing some of the excess liquid to thicken/evaporate.
✅This dish can be made up to a day ahead of time and refrigerated, tightly wrapped in foil. When ready to bake, just place the covered gratin in the oven, adding about an extra 5-7 minutes of baking time to the dish (covered). 
✅Shredded fontina, Swiss, comté, gouda, and mild cheddar cheese all make great cheese alternatives for gruyere.
✅Whole milk or half and half can be used in place of cream, although there will be more liquid pooled in the bottom of the gratin after it’s baked.
✅Turnips and rutabaga make great root vegetable alternatives for any of the three used in this recipe.

♨️Preheat oven to 400˚F (205 C). Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes or until vegetables are soft. Uncover gratin and top with shredded gruyere (optional). Place gratin back into oven, uncovered, and continue to bake for an additional 18 to 20 minutes or until vegetables are fork tender, cheese has melted and the top has lightly browned.

RECIPE: peach upside down cake🍑 recreating my most viral video and recipe a year later. trust me when I say this is the perfect summer cake to bake! enjoy and let me know if you give this recipe a try.😍
.
CAKE BATTER:
8 tbsp softened butter
1 cup cane sugar
2 tbsp sour cream or yogurt
2 eggs
1 1/4 cup + 2 tbsp all purpose flour
1 3/4 tsp baking powder
1/2 tsp salt
1 tsp cinnamon 
1/2 cup milk 
1 tsp vanilla extract
ASSEMBLY:
2/3 cup white sugar
1/3 cup water
3 peaches, (6 round slices total)
.
Preheat your oven to 350°F. Cream together the butter and sugar. Add yogurt then eggs one at a time and mix until smooth. In a separate bowl, whisk your flour, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon. Whisk your milk and extract in a separate jug. Add 1/3 of the dry mixture to the butter mixture and mix to combine. Add 1/2 the milk mixture and mix to combine. Repeat until both the dry and milk mixtures are all incorporated (making sure to finish on the dry mixture). Grease an 8” pan with nonstick cooking spray and line with a parchment round. In a small sauce pan add the sugar and water. Turn the stove on medium heat, swirling the pan constantly until the caramel comes to a boil and reaches an amber shade. Place your peaches face down on the greased, parchment lined pan. Pour the caramel over the peaches. Scoop the batter over the caramel covered peaches and spread out. Bake the upside down cake in the preheated oven for 35-40 minutes or until the top springs back to the touch. When the cake comes out of the oven, run around the sides of the pan with an offset spatula to release the edges. Let the cake cool for 10 minutes, and then invert it onto a serving plate. Enjoy!🤍

Stanley Tucci’s Favorite Zucchini Pasta: Spaghetti alla Nerano 🥒 

I was slightly skeptical of this, but it’s absolutely delicious. I highly suggest adding lemon and red pepper, really takes it up a notch. Here’s how to make it:

Olive oil
2 garlic cloves, crushed
2-3 small zucchini
Flakey salt
1/2 lb spaghetti (plus pasta water)
1-2 T butter
Parmesan cheese, freshly grated, about 3/4 cup (to taste)
4-5 basil leaves, torn
Black pepper
Lemon juice
Red pepper

1. In a large sauté pan, heat a generous amount of olive oil over medium/low heat. (You don’t need the zucchini to be completely submerged in oil). Throw in your garlic cloves and let that flavor the oil as it heats. Once it begins to sizzle, remove from the pan and discard.

2. Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add in your pasta and cook until al dente. Reserve about a cup of pasta water. 

3. Fry in your zucchini in batches, you don’t want to overcrowd the pan. You can stir/flip occasionally, until lightly golden brown. Remove and let drain on a paper towel-lined dish. Immediately hit them with some flakey salt. Repeat with your remaining zucchini. 

4. Once you’ve finished frying your zucchini, remove the oil from the pan. 

5. Add your zucchini back into the dry pan along with a splash of pasta water and your al dente pasta directly from the pot. 

6. Throw in a couple knobs of butter, another splash of pasta water, and your basil. Stir. 

6. Add in parmesan cheese, more butter, and more pasta. Stir. 

7. Continuing adding more cheese, butter, and pasta water until your sauce is silky and clings to the pasta. Just eyeball it here, you don’t need to be exact with your measurements.

7. Add in some freshly cracked black pepper (taste for salt), serve, and top with lemon juice and red pepper. Enjoy!

For the carrots:

For the chickpeas:
1 jar/can of chickpeas

Salt + pepper 

For serving:
1/2 cup plain greek yogurt 
2-3 oz feta

Chili-infused olive oil

Mango Habanero Salmon Crudo
Serves 2

Ingredients

Salmon:
1 lb sushi-grade salmon
2 tablespoons kosher salt
2 tablespoons granulated sugar
Zest of 1 lime
Zest of 1 lemon
Zest of 1 orange or tangerine

For the Sauce:
1/2 cup lime juice
2 tablespoons white soy sauce
1/4 cup mango, diced
1 habanero, seeded and chopped

Garnish:
Orange or tangerine supremes
Mango slices
Red onions, brunoise 
Chives, chopped
Maldon sea salt
Olive oil

Instructions

1. In a small bowl, combine 2 tablespoons of kosher salt, 2 tablespoons of granulated sugar, lime zest, lemon zest, and tangerine zest.

3. Blend together the lime juice, white soy sauce, diced mango, and habanero until smooth. Strain the sauce through a fine mesh strainer and chill in the refrigerator until ready to serve.

4. Slice the salmon thinly, about 1/8 inch, and arrange on a plate. Spoon the mango habanero sauce over the salmon slices.
 Garnish with orange or tangerine supremes, mango slices, thinly sliced red onions, chopped chives, Maldon sea salt, and a drizzle of olive oil. 

5. Serve immediately, as the acid from the sauce will alter the texture of the salmon the longer it sits.

Crusty White Loaf 🍞⬇️ (RECIPE)

Ingredients:

- 500g bread flour (or plain)
- 350g warm water
- 10g salty salty flavours
- 7g instant yeast

1. Mix all your ingredients into a shaggy dough

2. Tip out on a floured work surface and knead for 5-10 mins until smooth

3. Oil up a bowl and add the dough, cover and leave for 90 mins to double in size

4. Tip it out and push out all the air and shape into a flat rectangle

5. Now pull in the corners and tuck the dough in on itself until you have a sausage shape

6. Now add to a loaf tin or pan with flour and cover for 30 mins to double in size

7. Grab a big knife or blade and score down the middle

8. Add to your oven anything over 200 degrees C for 30 mins with a pan of warm water on the bottom shelf to help the crust

9. Take it out, remove from the tin and add back for 5 mins

10. Take it out, leave to cool for half hour and enjoy!!!

This dish is luxurious and delicious, yet it is so easy to make 🔥 Full recipe below…

Serves 4

- 30g parmesan, grated
- 30g basil leaves
- 40g walnuts, toasted
- 1 garlic clove (leave this out if on an actual first date, trust)
- 130g spinach
- Black pepper and sea salt to season

- 1 leek, finely chopped
- 40g unsalted butter
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 2 medium garlic cloves, sliced
- Salt and pepper

- 300g orzo
- 900ml stock

- 4 salmon fillets
- High heat oil for frying
- Fine sea salt
- Sour cream
- Dill
- Lemon zest and juice

1. Place the salmon fillets onto a baking tray with a rack, sprinkle both sides with the fine sea salt and leave in the fridge until ready to cook.
2. Toast the walnuts in a dry pan until golden brown and fragrant.
3. Blanch the spinach leaves in boiling water for 20 seconds then cool in an ice bath to stop them cooking. Squeeze out excess moisture once cooled.
4. To make the pesto, add the parmesan, basil, walnuts, garlic, spinach, salt and pepper into a blender. Blitz until smooth.
5. Add the leeks, butter and oil into a pan. Cook for 5 minutes over a medium-high heat until softened and starting to caramelise.
6. Add the Orzo and stock, bring to a simmer, then cover and cook for 15 minutes on low heat. Add an extra splash of water if needed halfway through.

8. Remove salmon from the fridge then pat the skin dry.

10. To serve, add the salmon on top of a bowl of orzo with a dollop of sour cream, freshly chopped dill and some lemon zest and juice. Enjoy!

Temari sushi with Pickled Cucumber and Radish

Celebrate International Sushi Day with top quality Akita Komachi rice from @yutakaeats - Famous for its sweetness in flavour & the perfect amount of moisture & stickiness. Full of flavour even when cold, this rice is great for bento boxes & rice balls.

Such a pretty type of sushi, Temari rice balls are unique & pretty to make at home. No need for fish or seafood, plenty of colour from veggies pickled in the same sushi-su you use to make the rice.

- Serves 4 -

INGREDIENTS
1 square of cellophane or cut sandwich bag
A bowl of cold water for your fingers
2 Snap-packs of Yutaka Akitakomachi rice (300g)
400 mls Cold water
150 mls Yutaka Rice Vinegar
3 tbsp Sugar
1 tbsp Salt
200g Fresh radishes
1/2 a Cucumber
Micro-herbs, dill, sesame seeds

METHOD
Open 2 snap-packs & soak the rice in a medium pan (ideally with a glass lid) with the water for 30 mins.

Prep the sushi-su. Mix the rice vinegar with the sugar & salt. Stir until clear. Set to one side.

Slice radishes & cucumber thinly. Use a slicer, like a mandolin. Be careful!

Pickle the cucumber with 3 tbsp (45 mls) of the sushi-su mixture in a bowl. Same for the radishes, with another 3 tbsp (45 mls) of sushi-su. Leave them to pickle whilst you cook the sushi rice. You’ll have 4 tbsp (60 mls) for the sushi rice.

In the water that it soaked in, bring the rice to the boil and simmer with the lid on for 12 mins. Turn off the heat & leave it for 5 mins longer, lid on.

Turn out the rice into a baking tray or large flat pan. Add sushi-su & fan, folding the rice, to cool it.

Place a sheet of cling film on the palm of your hand, & put a few slices of your pickles on top. Wet the fingers of your other hand in the bowl of water, & shake off any excess. It stops the sushi rice sticking.

Take a spoonful of rice (20g approx.) & place it on top of the pickles.

Bring the edges of the cling film into the centre, over the rice, & shape into a tight ball, then twist & close over the top. Unwrap and plate. Repeat with remaining ingredients.

Garnish with micro herbs, dill & Yutaka’s roasted sesame seeds.

Serves 2

▫️1 lemon, zest

In an ovenproof pan, heat 1 tbsp oil and fry off the leek until softened, 4 minutes. Then, add in the garlic and asparagus and cook for a further 2-3 minutes. Follow with the peas and lemon zest. Season well. 
In a blender, add the stock cube, spinach and boiling water. Blend until it becomes a vibrant green sauce (it won’t be completely smooth). 
Stir the green sauce into the pan. Add the herbs, season again, then make wells to crack the eggs into. Place the lid on the pan and reduce heat to low. Cook for 8 minutes with the lid on for an entirely hob-based option, or for even better results place the pan (without lid) into the oven for the final 2 minutes, until the egg whites are set. 
Top with extra herbs, lemon zest, chilli flakes and lots of feta. Devour with crusty bread and ENJOY! 🤍

Recipe 👇🏾How to make the easiest carrot rice 🥕 🍚 

Ingredients:
5 tbsps olive oil
1 carrot, grated
1/2 onion, chopped
2 cups of basmati rice
3 cups of water
1 stock cube
salt to taste

Method 
Wash and grate the carrot 
Chop the onion into small bits 
Measure out your rice and rinse several times in water until the water runs clear 
Pour olive oil into a pot and bring to medium-high heat (e.g level 7 on an induction/ceramic hob)
Fry the carrots and onion in the oil for about 5 minutes, stirring it every so often 
Add in the rice and fry for another 5 minutes, stirring it every so often 
Add in the water and once it starts boiling add the stock cube and salt to taste
Cover with a lid and cook on very low heat for 15 minutes (e.g level 3 on an induction/ceramic hob)

Tips
In general to cook rice You don’t really need to measure just use the ratio of 1 part rice to 1.5 parts of water 
Cover the rice with tin foil, so it keeps the moisture in during cooking 
Add water in bit by bit depending on the type of rice you may need less than you think 
Taste the water whilst you add in the salt so you don’t over-salt it

CRISPY ‘DUCK’ PANCAKES 🍄

It was my first time growing my own KING OYSTER MUSHROOMS, so I had to make something special…

CRISPY DUCK PANCAKES were my favourite chinese dish back in the day. And honestly, this plant-based version using mushrooms is a gamechanger 🤯

It’s SO easy, very quick, really fun, and also absolutely delicious - and TASTES SO SIMILAR TO DUCK IT’S A JOKE 🤩

Full recipe written below - shout out to @sophiewyburd + @mob for the recipe inspo, been meaning to try this for YEARS. AND to @marvellousmushrooms for the wonderful grow kit 🙏

INGREDIENTS (serves 4)

500g king oyster / oyster mushrooms
4 tbsp cornflour
2 tbsp chinese five spice
1 tbsp garlic powder
1 tbsp onion powder
150g hoisin sauce
1 cucumber
Bunch of spring onions
Toasted sesame seeds
Chinese pancakes
Salt
Pepper
Vegetable Oil

METHOD

1. With your hands, tear the mushrooms into small thin strips. Place in a large mixing bowl. 
2. Add the cornflour, five spice, onion + garlic, then season with salt + pepper. Mix well to make sure everything is well coated. 
3. In a frying pan, warm up enough oil to cover the bottom of the pan on a medium high heat. 
4. Add a handful of mushrooms, making sure not to overcrowd the pan. Fry until browned + crisp on both sides, then place on kitchen towel to drain excess oil. Repeat for the rest of the mushrooms. 
5. Once all the mushrooms are cooked, place in a bowl + stir through 2 tbsp of hoisin sauce. 
6. Chop your cucumber + spring onion into strips, warm up your pancakes, then serve - pancake, some hoisin sauce, mushrooms, veg, sesame seeds if you like, more sauce + enjoy!

Creamy basque cheesecake made with a food processor🤍 This one tastes even better after a couple of days in the fridge. 

You can also make this by hand or using a stand mixer. Just make sure all the ingredients are at room temp.

Recipe:
650g cream cheese block, cut into cubes
195g sugar
1 tsp vanilla extract (optional)
4g cornstarch
2g salt
180g eggs
250g whipping cream

1. Preheat the oven to 240C. Place the cream cheese, sugar, vanilla, cornstarch and salt into a bowl of food processor. Blend on a low speed until smooth. Make sure to scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl in between to make a homogeneous mixture.
2. Add the eggs and mix on a low speed until fully incorporated.
3. Add the whipping cream and mix slowly until well combined. Strain the mixture through a fine sieve. 
4. Pour the batter into a 8 inch cake pan lined with parchment paper, then tap the pan against a work surface a few times to eliminate air bubbles. Bake at 230C for about 23-25 minutes. The cake should be jiggly in the center when you remove it from the oven.
5. Cool the cake in the pan on a rack until room temperature, then refrigerate overnight.

Serves 2

2 tbsp olive oil + extra for greasing 
1 x 500g pack gnocchi 
2 sausages, skins removed 
400g cherry tomatoes, most halved 
½ bulb fennel, roughly chopped 
½ red onion, roughly chopped 
2 handfuls of finely chopped basil leaves 
1 clove garlic, crushed 
The juice of ¼ lemon 
10g Pine nuts 
Parm to serve 
Salt and pepper 


1. Preheat the oven to 180c fan. Rub a little oil all over the base of a 24cm x 32cm baking tray. Chuck the gnocchi, cherry tomatoes, fennel, onion, 1 tbsp oil and a good pinch of salt and pepper into the tray. Mix well. Rip the sausages into tiny pieces over the top and pour in 60ml of water. Roast for 25 minutes, enough time to cook the sauces and soften the veg. Remove from the oven and give the pan a shake. This is really to loosen everything and get the tomatoes to break down even more. If it looks dry, add another 40-50ml of water and return to the oven for 10-15 minutes or until crispy on the top. 
2.Meanwhile, mix the basil garlic, lemon, a pinch of salt and with the remaining oil.
3. Give the tray a really good shake to loosen everything and get the tomatoes to burst even more, coating the gnocchi. It’s not a saucy dish but the gnocchi should be coated with the juices from the veg, some bits soft and some crispy. Check the seasoning and add more salt and pepper to taste.
4. To serve, drizzle the herb oil over the traybake, scatter over the pine nuts, and rain down some Parm. Get your forks and dive on in.

Welcome back to my Cypriot Kitchen Classics

Today we’re making patatosalata - a version of my mum’s Cypriot potato salad. 

INGREDIENTS
800g baby potatoes, peeled 2-3 spring onions, finely sliced 1 handful, about 1/8 cup finely chopped fresh parsley 1 handful, about 1/8 cup finely chopped fresh coriander 1-2 garlic cloves, grated 1 tablespoon lemon zest, grated 60ml lemon juice 1 teaspoon dried mint 75ml EVOO salt flakes freshly cracked black pepper
METHOD
In a large pot, bring water and 2 tablespoons of salt to a boil. Add the potatoes to the boiling water and return to a boil. Reduce the heat to a simmer and cook for 10-15 minutes or until the potatoes are fork-tender but still hold their shape. Avoid overcooking. Once cooked, drain the potatoes and allow them to cool slightly while you prepare the dressing.  In a large salad bowl, combine the sliced spring onions, chopped parsley, chopped coriander, grated garlic, lemon zest, lemon juice, dried mint, and extra virgin olive oil. Mix well to incorporate.  Add the slightly cooled, quartered potatoes to the dressing. Gently toss until the potatoes are evenly coated with the dressing. Season with salt flakes and freshly cracked black pepper to taste. Adjust as needed.  Enjoy the potato salad warm or at room temperature.  Note: If not serving immediately, reserve the spring onions and fresh herbs and add them to the potatoes once cooled and ready to serve to maintain their freshness and vibrant appearance.

Serves 2

1. Preheat oven to 180c fan. Dry the lentils with kitchen paper and chuck them into a roasting tin. Add 1 tbsp of oil and toss together. Spread out and roast for 18-20 minutes or until crispy.

5. Cook the pak choi for 2 mins in pan of boiling water. Remove and add the noodles to the pan. Cook for 4-5 minutes or until al dente. Scoop out a little noodle water and drain. Divide the noodles between the two serving bowls and spoon 2 tbsp of noodle water over each. Add the pak choi.
7. Just before serving, toss the crispy lentils into the mushrooms. Spoon over the noodles and serve with spring onions on top and extra chilli oil

CAULIFLOWER STEAK + CHIMICHURRI 🔥

of my favourite ways to cook cauliflower is to cut it into steaks, then serve with chimichurri + a creamy butter bean purée.

it sounds fancy, but it’s actually super easy to make, comes together in no time at all & uses only simple, plant-based ingredients 🌱

I’ve written the full recipe out for you below so enjoy & let me know if you give it a go 👇

INGREDIENTS (serves 2)

CAULI

2 cauliflower steaks (from 1 large cauli)
1 tbsp smoked paprika 
3 garlic cloves
2 tbsp butter 
Salt
Pepper
Olive oil

CHIMICHURRI

Large bunch of parsley 
1 garlic clove 
1 red chilli
2 tbsp red wine vinegar
100ml extra virgin olive oil
Salt
Pepper

BUTTER BEAN PURÉE

700g jarred butter beans
1 lemon
1 garlic clove 
2 tbsp nutritional yeast
Salt
Pepper

METHOD

1. First, make the chimichurri. Finely chop the fresh herbs, then add to a mixing bowl. Finely dice the chilli, mince the garlic + add to the herbs with the vinegar. Season to taste, then stream in the olive oil whilst mixing until throughly combined. Set aside.
2. For the butter beans, simply pour  into a blender with the juice of a lemon, salt, pepper, 1 garlic clove + nutritional yeast. 
3. For the cauliflower, chop into steaks- you should be able to get two from the middle of a large one. Save the extra florets for another recipe, or roast with salt, pepper, paprika + olive oil to serve alongside the steaks.
4. Chop up the leaves + stems & set aside for a zero-waste garnish. 
5. Season the steaks with salt, pepper + paprika on both sides, then drizzle with oil + massage well.
6. Heat a frying pan to medium high. Add 2 tbsp olive oil. Once hot, add the steak - press down to sear. After several minutes, flip + fry other side until golden brown. 
7. Bash the garlic cloves, add with the butter + baste continuously. Once the steaks are cooked, remove from the pan + add the chopped leaves/stems with a splash more oil & cook until golden + crisp.
8. To serve, pour the bean purée into the middle of a plate. Place the steak on top, drizzle with chimichurri & scatter over the cauli leaves.

Brown Butter Turkish Eggs

100g butter
3 cloves garlic, sliced thin
1 small shallot, sliced thin
1 tbsp Aleppo pepper
150g Greek yoghurt
5g mint
Juice of half a lemon 
3 eggs, poached
Salt and pepper
Toasted sourdough

1. Simmer the butter in a pan until brown.

7. When you’re ready to serve place three good dollops of the herbed yogurt on a plate or bowl.
8. Follow that up with the eggs and then spoon over the chilli butter.
9. Top with a little more chopped mint and serve with toasted sourdough.

Croustillants patate douce et feta 🌿🍠 thym, romarin, miel et sésame 🍯 

La feta dans la pâte filo, on sait déjà que c’est délicieux (avec le miel et les graines de sésame bien-sûr 🙊). Mais avec la patate douce en plus, c’est encore meilleur 🤤🙈. (C’est une vieille recette mais je vous rappelle l’existence de ces petites choses 🥰). On peut aussi donner une forme de cigares en taillant la fêta et la patate douce en bâtonnets. Et si on aime pas la feta, le fromage de chèvre passe bien aussi même si ça ne vaut pas la feta 🙄😅.

🌿 feuilles de pâte filo (selon besoins)
🌿 huile d’olive
🌿 1 grosse patate douce
🌿 1 bloc de feta ici mais c’est selon besoins (1 = 4 pièces comme ici ou 6/7 cigares)
🌿 sel, thym, romarin, paprika fumé ou paprika, piment d’Espelette en option
🌿 miel
🌿 graines de sésame 

Éplucher et tailler la patate douce en tranches assez épaisses. Quadriller en surface, disposer sur une plaque couverte de papier cuisson. Badigeonner d’un peu d’huile dessus/dessous et assaisonner avec sel, paprika, thym, romarin et une touche de piment d’Espelette en option. Enfourner 25 min dans le four préchauffé à 190º.
Couper les morceaux de feta. Disposer sur les tranches et les tailler selon la forme des morceaux de feta (les chutes de patate douce sont parties dans un bowl quinoa). Ajouter la touche de miel sauf si vous préférez le mettre après cuisson, le thym et le romarin. Badigeonner une feuille filo d’huile (ou beurre fondu), plier en deux, badigeonner à nouveau légèrement . Disposer le morceau feta/patate douce, rabattre les côtés dans la longueur puis plier. Couper si un morceau dépasse, la fermeture doit se trouver dessous. Mettre sur une plaque, badigeonner légèrement d’huile, parsemer de graines de sésame et enfourner 10 min à 200°. Surveiller. Déguster avec un beau filet de miel 🥰.

RECIPE🍳⁣
⁣

Goat Cheese quiche with potato crust. 

This cheese and veggie packed quiche can be made for breakfast, brunch or even dinner. It has a crispy potato crust instead of pie crust. And it is loaded with fresh vegetables! 

Ingredients: 

1-2 large Russet Potatoes, thinly sliced 
3 Tbsp. Oil, such as avocado oil, divided
1 onion, chopped
1 C. Spinach, chopped
Salt and pepper
2 Garlic cloves, minced 
1 Zucchini, chopped
Handful of Asparagus, cut into small pieces 
6 eggs
6 oz Goat cheese
1/2 C.  Parmesan cheese, shredded 
1/2 C. Milk
1/2 tsp. Oregano 

Method: 

Preheat oven to 375 degrees F. Toss the sliced potatoes into a bowl with 2 Tablespoons of oil and some salt and pepper to taste.  Taking one slice of potato at a time, start lining the edges of a pie pan, making sure the potatoes are slightly over lapping each other.  Once the edge of the pan is lined, start laying the potatoes on the bottom of the pie dish, starting on the outside edge and working your way in, again making sure to overlap the potatoes slightly. Once done, place the potatoes in the oven for 20-25 minutes. While the potato crust is in the oven, heat the remaining 1 Tablespoon of oil in a skillet. Add the zucchini, onion, asparagus. Sauté veggies for 6-7 minutes or until they just start to become tender. Stir in the garlic and cook 1-2 more minutes. Remove from heat and stir in spinach, salt, pepper and oregano. 

In a large bowl, combine the eggs, salt, pepper and milk together. Whisk until combined. Stir in goat cheese. 

When the potato crust in done, pour the sautéed veggies into pie pan and spread them out evenly. Top with the egg and goat cheese mixture. Sprinkle on the shredded Parmesan cheese. Place in the oven for 30-40 minutes or until the eggs are set and cooked. Let cool slightly before enjoying!

Parmigiana a ventaglio 🪭 

Ingredients:

2 aubergines 
550g  tomato passata, rustic
2 cloves of garlic
Green onion stalks
Basil leaves
Olive oil
Salt, Pepper
60 g nduja 
Chili flakes,optional
2 balls of mozzarella, 125 g each)
Parmesan, grated 
6 tbsp semolina 

Instructions:

Preheat your oven to 190°C (375°F) with fan on. Slice the aubergines lengthwise from the stem to the bottom at approximately 1 cm intervals. Gently press them down to spread a little then salt generously. For better dehydration, Let them drain for about 15 minutes, then pat dry, or you can place them directly into the oven if preferred.

Bake the aubergines for about 35 minutes or until done to preference.

Prepare the tomato sauce by heating some olive oil in a suitable pot and briefly sauté the garlic cloves and green onion stalks over medium heat.

Add the tomatoes and simmer until the aubergines are done, allowing the sauce to thicken. 

Remove the aubergines from the oven and let them cool slightly, drizzle with olive oil, and coat both sides with semolina.
Sear them in a hot pan on both sides for about 2-3 minutes until golden brown, being careful not to burn them.

Insert mozzarella between the aubergine slices and return to the oven for an additional 10 minutes or until the cheese has slightly browned.

Once the tomato sauce has reduced, remove the garlic and green onion pieces, then add the nduja and basil. Season with salt and pepper, and if necessary, a teaspoon of sugar to balance the acidity.

To serve, plate the sauce, place the baked aubergine on top, and sprinkle with grated Parmesan. Garnish with additional basil leaves and optional chili flakes.

Did you know you can make an orange cake using a blender? Super easy, soft and delicious! 🍊🧡

Save this recipe for when you need to make last-minute cake. 

Recipe:
1 seedless orange (unpeeled and preferably organic)
250 g flour (2 cups)
3 eggs 
200 g sugar (1 cup)
16 g baking powder 
90 ml vegetable oil (like sunflower oil) (1/3 cup + 1 tbsp)
60 ml milk (regular or plant based) (1/4 cup)
1 tsp vanilla extract 

Steps: 

1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (180°C). Grease and cover in parchment paper a 7 inch (18 cm) cake pan. 

2. Pick a type of orange that has a thin zest like navel oranges. Wash the whole orange thoroughly, remove the extremities at the top and the bottom where the zest tends to be a bit hard. Cut it into pieces and place the orange in the blender.

3. To the blender, add sugar, vegetable oil, milk, and eggs.

4. Blend the ingredients until you achieve a smooth, orange-infused mixture and then sift in the powders (flour and baking powder). Blend for a short amount of time to quickly incorporate the powders without over mixing too much. 

5. Pour the batter into the prepared cake pan.

6. Bake in the preheated oven for approximately 45 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.

7. Allow the cake to cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then decorate it with icing sugar. Slice, serve, and savor the citrusy goodness!

The Caramelised Onions & Goat’s Cheese One

This is the recipe for the batter. If you’d like the recipe for the caramelised onions I have that on my website in UK & US measurements. Comment below with the word ‘onions’ and I’ll send you a link to it.

4 eggs
180g milk
90g plain flour
1/4 tsp salt
40g butter 
1g fresh basil
1 garlic clove
150g goat’s cheese

1. Preheat the oven to 230°C.
2. In a stick blender jug add the eggs, flour, milk & salt. Blend until smooth and aerated.
3. Leave the mixture to stand whilst the oven comes up to temperature. The closer the mix is to room temp, the better rise you’ll get in the finished product.
4. Caramelise your onions (for the link to this recipe, comment below with the word ‘onions’ and I’ll send you a link).
5. Chiffonade the basil, mince the garlic and break up half the goat cheese into a bowl with a pinch of salt.
6. When you’re ready to go, place the pan in the oven for around 10 minutes to get ripping hot.
7. Remove the pan from the oven and add the butter. Let it bubble and melt down completely. Then pour your batter mix into the pan.
8. Scatter the cheese and herb mix over the top and return to the oven for 15 minutes. Do not open the oven during this time.
9. Top your Dutch baby with the onions (they can be warmed up again if you like), scatter the rest of the goat’s cheese which will melt on the onions.
10. I like to also top with some whole basil leaves, pepper and red chilli flakes.

French Onion Tarte Tatin…so simple but luxurious, the tarte is very easy to prepare but so elegant…back in my good old restaurant days we had an individual version of this and it was a hit!

Got the idea of the dijon mustard on the crust from serious eats btw!

Ingredients:
3 large yellow onions (2 cut into thick wedges as shown in the video and 1 sliced).
2 shallots (thinly sliced).
1 large red onion (thinly sliced).
1/3 cup beef stock or demi glace (I used demi).
2 tbsp balsamic vinegar.
1/3 cup red wine.
1/2 tsp nutmeg.
1/4 tsp cayenne pepper.
1/2 tsp fresh or dried thyme.
2 tbsp chives.
Salt/pepper to taste.
3 tbsp unsalted butter.
3 tbsp cane sugar.
1 cup grated comte or dijon.
1 tbsp grainy Dijon mustard.

Shortcrust:
2 cups flour.
8 tbsp butter.
6 tbsp cold water.
1 tsp salt.

Glaze:
½ cup red wine.
½ cup beef stock or demi glace.
1 tbsp balsamic vinegar.
4 tbsp cold butter.

Directions:
1. Add flour, butter and salt to a food processor and start pulsing adding in the cold water 1 tbsp at a time. It should be crumbly. Form it into a flat circle and refrigerate covered in plastic wrap for at least 2 hrs.
2. Add the shallots, red onion and sliced yellow onion to your saucier with a bit of olive oil, brown on medium low for 20 min. Add a pinch of salt, wine, stock, balsamic, cayenne, nutmeg and thyme. Cook on medium low, stirring often until most of the liquid is absorbed, about 10 min. Finish with 1 tbsp butter.
3. Roll out the crust and cut to fit the pan, fold edges a bit, pierce with a fork and rub the Dijon on it.
4. Spread the 2 tbsp butter onto the 10 inch skillet & add sugar. Arrange onion wedges as shown in video. Brown for about 6-8 min or until the sugar becomes golden. Fill in the gaps of the onion wedges with the caramelized onion, cook 1-2 min. Top with gruyere and the crust.
5. Bake at 400F for 35-45 min.
6. Boil the wine, balsamic and stock for the glaze until reduced to 1/3. Turn heat off and whisk in cold butter.
7. Flip the tarte tatin almost immediately, if the sugar cools off too much it can stick. Add the glaze and chives.

This is your Christmas morning one pan breakfast: the Smoked Salmon Savoury Dutch Baby.
 
I’m using the pure cast iron skillet from the @stellarkitchenware new Cast range. It’s 25cm which is the perfect size for this Dutch Baby.

It’s made in the UK from 100% recycled cast iron and comes pre-seasoned twice for a naturally non-stick surface. The extra thick base provides efficient and uniform heat diffusion.

If you’ve never heard of a Dutch Baby before, it’s like a cross between a pancake and a Yorkshire pudding. They’re more eggy than a Yorkshire and are originally made to be sweet, filled with fruit, cream or whatever you want.

But they’re also not Dutch! They are based on the crepe-like German pancake called pfannkuchen. Named by a mispronunciation of “Deutsch” (meaning German) as “Dutch”.

1/4 of this recipe was perfect for breakfast/brunch for me. It’s actually quite light and will leave room for Christmas Day chocolates and dinner later on.

Home Cooking Sessions: Parmigiana Di Melanzane. A breaded version of the southern Italian classic. Full recipe below! 👇🏽🇮🇹
-
1. Thinly slice your aubergine, then sprinkle over some sea salt and let sit for ~45 mins - this will draw out some of its excess water 
2. Rinse off the salt, then pat dry and start breading 
3. You can either just dust in flour, or do a 3-stage process like this. I tried this way for the first time and actually prefer just flour! 
4. For this recipe though, dust in flour, then beaten eggs, then panko and set aside 
5. Add a generous glug of EV olive oil to a pan and bring to med-high, then place in 2-3 of your aubergine cutlets at a time and fry till golden - basting and flipping throughout 
6. Once crispy, set aside, season and repeat 
7. For the sauce, add 1 finely diced shallot, 2 cloves sliced garlic, peperoncino and parsley stems to a pan laced with olive oil and fry on med heat for ~3 mins 
8. Add in ~750 of tomato passata and season with sea salt, black pepp + 1tsp sugar, followed by chopped basil - cook on low for ~20 mins then set aside 
9. Assembly: add some sauce to a baking dish, followed by your aubergine, more sauce, fresh basil, powdered parmigiano Reggiano + fresh & dried mozzarella 
10. Repeat the process until the top layer which is just tomato sauce, plenty of cheese and some ev olive oil 
11. Bake at 180c for 30-45 mins until golden and bubbling, then rest for the same time before serving
-

MUSHROOM DONER 🌯

everyone loves a doner kebab, but did you know that you could make your own at home, in just 30 minutes, but entirely made from PLANTS 🤯

AD| for this kebab, I’ve teamed up with @morewithmushrooms and instead of using meat, we’re using MUSHROOMS, which are naturally super meaty in texture 🍄

I served up my mushroom doner in a wrap with tzatziki, pickled cabbage, salad, tahini + chilli sauce - but you can use whichever kebab fillings you like!

I’ll leave the full recipe 👇 let me know if you give it a go x

INGREDIENTS (serves 4)

MUSHROOM DONER:

8 large flat mushrooms
1tbsp each of: smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, dried oregano, ground cumin, lemon juice
3tbsp olive oil
Salt & pepper

TZATZIKI:

1 grated cucumber
250g vegan yoghurt
2 crushedgarlic cloves
30g fresh mint / dill
Juice of 1 lemon
1tbsp extra virgin olive oil
Salt & pepper

TO SERVE:

4 wraps
2 beef tomatoes
1/2 white onion
1/4 red cabbage (pickled)
Handful fresh parsley
4tbsp tahini
4tbsp chilli sauce

METHOD

1. To make the shawarma paste, combine the seasonings, lemon juice + olive oil. Season with salt + pepper, then mix well. 
2. Carefully coat each of the mushrooms in the paste, making more paste as needed.
3. To cook the mushrooms, stack up on skewers, then roast in the oven at 220 for 30 minutes, or until charred & cooked through. 
4. Slice the mushroom doner with a sharp knife, then get your salads + sauces ready - combine all the tzatziki ingredients + mix well. 
5. Warm the wraps, then assemble - garlic sauce, salad, mushroom shawarma, tahini & chilli sauce, then fresh parsley. 

Enjoy!

Focaccia - onions, blue cheese and confit garlic

Ingredients:
- 500g (17.6 oz) flour
- 4g salt
- 4g sugar
- 7g yeast
- 325g (11.5 fl oz) water
- 2 onions, sliced thick
- 25 cloves of garlic, peeled
- olive oil
- 100g (3.5 oz) blue cheese

Method:
1. In the bowl of a stand mixer (or just a normal bowl if you don’t have a mixer), add the flour, salt, sugar, and yeast, and whisk.
2. Next, add the hook attachment (or wooden spoon) and turn to medium, stream in room temperature water and mix until the dough comes together and is smooth. This should take about 7-8 minutes in a mixer.
3. Turn the dough onto a floured surface and bring it together into a ball, then grease the mixing bowl with some olive oil and place the dough back into the bowl, cover with a clean tea towel and leave in a warm spot to proof for an hour or until it has doubled in size.
4. Once doubled, turn out and fold it on itself, then in an oven dish drizzle 3-4 tablespoons of olive oil and place the dough into the dish.
5. Push the dough out so it stretches to all the sides, cover the dish and leave the dough to prove again for an hour.
6. While that is proving, place the garlic into an oven-safe dish with some thyme, salt, and olive oil, and bake at 140°C (284°F) for 40 minutes, remove and leave to cool at room temperature.
7. Preheat your oven to 200°C (392°F).
8. Take the thick-sliced onions and place them onto an oven tray, drizzle with oil and season with salt on both sides.
9. Bake in the 200°C (392°F) oven for 10-12 minutes or until cooked through and starting to soften.
10. Once the dough has proven, drizzle some of the warm garlic oil on top and use your fingertips to poke a bunch of holes into the dough.
11. Use these holes to add the confit garlic, then top with the onions and blue cheese.
12. Bake at 200°C (392°F) for 25 minutes or until the bread is cooked and golden brown on top.

Crispy Rice Salad 🥗 one of my favourite ways to use up leftover rice, herbs and veggies at the end of the week!

This recipe takes some inspiration from the Laotian Nam Khao - a crispy rice salad dish packed with fragrant spices and herbs. Made this slightly healthier by baking the rice rather than pan frying it, and just chopped and chucked in any leftover herbs and salad greens I had from the fridge. Give this one a go if you're looking for a crispy tasty way to use up those leftover greens! 💚

Recipe 👇 

Ingredients
2 cups cooked rice
3 Tbsp oil
2 Tbsp thai red curry paste 
1-1.5 cups of chopped herbs and greens (I had coriander, mint, spring onions and baby rocket)
1 red onion (sliced)
3 birds eye chillis (sliced) (optional)
1 garlic clove (minced)
3cm ginger (minced)
2 tsp sugar
1-2 Tbsp fish sauce
Juice from 1 lime
Garnish: roasted peanuts

Method
1) Preheat oven to 200C. In a large mixing bowl, mix rice, curry paste and oil until well combined. Spread over a lined baking tray and bake for 35-40 minutes,  stirring halfway.
2) Make your sauce by mixing together the garlic, ginger, sugar, fish sauce and lime juice. Taste and balance - it should taste sweet, sour and salty. Set aside.
3) Once the crispy rice is done, add to a large bowl then top with your chopped herbs and greens, red onion and chillis (if using). Pour sauce over and toss through. Top with roasted peanuts and enjoy!

Blanch and drain the peas refreshing them in cold water. Place half the peas in a large mixing bowl and using the base of a glass roughly smash them. 
 
Grate the courgette using the course side of a grated and give it a good squeeze to release some of the liquid into a bowl. Discard the liquid. 
 
Add the squeezed courgetti to the smashed peas with the remaining whole peas, spring onion, oregano, dill, lemon zest, a good pinch of salt and the eggs. Mix to combine.
 
In a separate bowl whisk together the flour and baking powder, then fold half into the batter to loosen it, followed by the remaining half. 
 
Heat enough oil to coat the bottom of a frying pan over a medium heat. 
 
When the oil is hot, drop roughly a heaped tbsp per fritter into the pan. I tend to start with 3. Use the back of the spoon to flatten the fritters and fry for about 3 mins either side until golden brown. 
 
Transfer the cooked fritters to a tray lined with kitchen towel and work in batches. 
 
For the dill yogurt, combine all the ingredients in a bowl. Serve alongside the fritters.

4. Dress the spelt with the rocket pesto (keep a little aside to dress the plate 
5. Muddle together the pumpkin, rocket leaves & dressed spelt in a bowl. Tear over the mozzarella and top with hazelnuts & the rest of the pesto

Zucchini Scarpaccia 🌱🇮🇹
⠀
Summer is coming to an end, but here is one last recipe to say goodbye 💛
⠀
Originating in Camaiore (Tuscany), “Scarpaccia di Zucchine“ is an Italian classic, using simple ingredients and making the most of it! I first saw this recipe at @cosatipreparopercena 🤗
⠀
RECIPE (1 large tray)
- 1 kg zucchini (3-4 medium, or pumpkin)
- 1 large onion
- 1.5 tsp salt
- 150 g all purpose flour (optionally add some cornmeal or chickpea flour)
- 1/2 tsp rosemary
- black pepper
- 2 tbsp olive oil
⠀
❶ Finely cut the zucchini and onion using a mandolin (or knife, if you don’t have one like me 🤷‍♂️)
❷ Transfer to a large bowl, mix in the salt and let it sit for about 2 hours, to draw out most of the moisture.
❸ Squeeze out most of the water, combine with flour, herbs and black pepper. Add more flour or water if needed, so you get the consistency of a pancake batter.
❹ Add the veggies to the batter and mix.
❺ Add to a well oiled baking tray and spread out evenly.
❻ Bake at 200°C for 30-50 minutes until caramelized and crispy.
❼ Cut into squares like a focaccia and enjoy as an aperativo or however you prefer!
⠀
TIPS
- the zucchini can also be swapped for pumpkin, making this a great fall dish!

Back from Sicily. This was one of the best things I ate last week. Such a simple combination, and so utterly delicious. If you don’t like anchovies, just skip them & make these onions as is, we’ve just eaten these for lunch, savouring every last mouthful, & if you could have told me I’d eat a tray of onions for lunch before last week, I’d never have believed you! I brought these Tropea onions in Palermo at the market at the weekend, the ladies in the kitchen @annatascalanza just used regular round red onions, both equally & insanely memorable. No exact recipe here, it’s that easy! Peel & slice into rings, season well with salt & plenty of black pepper, add a good amount of dried oregano, a good amount of olive oil & bake at 190C for around 30 ish mins, carefully flip, cook for another 10, until soft & burnished. Whip out of the oven & immediately douse with good red wine vinegar & drape 1/2 an anchovy over the top, to melt just a little. I think I will eat onions like this forever more.
